543988|2026-09.headline: Nuvama Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to about INR937 crores and operating PAT 26% to INR319 crores, with ROE near 29%.
543988|2026-09.overview: Revenue of about INR937 crores (+21% YoY) and operating PAT of about INR319 crores (+26% YoY) were driven by all segments, with Asset Services and Capital Markets contributing strongly. Client assets reached about INR5.5 lakh crores (+25%), with record net new money of INR3,300 crores in Wealth and INR5,000 crores in Private. A one-time post-tax charge of about INR16 crores came from pre-closing a venture debt fund, plus about INR9-10 crores of accelerated amortisation over 12 months. The board skipped the H1 FY27 dividend to manage debt-to-equity, currently about 2.9x against a 2.5x target.

financial_highlights.metric: One-time exceptional charge (venture debt fund pre-closure)

segments.name: Nuvama Wealth (MPIS)
segments.commentary: Client assets crossed about INR46,000 crores; Q2 net flows about INR3,300 crores and over INR6,000 crores in H1. Revenue growth was above 25% YoY in each of seven or eight quarters, moderated this quarter by a high base from a Q2 FY26 real estate co-invest. Lending book about INR6,000 crores, up about 60% YoY.

segments.name: Nuvama Private (ARR)
segments.commentary: ARR assets about INR60,000-62,000 crores; Q2 net new money about INR5,000 crores. ARR is about 64% of revenue. Lending book grew about 50% on H1 basis with NII up about 50%. Transaction income of INR80-90 crores per quarter treated as run rate.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: AUM about INR12,000 crores. Commercial real estate fund about 50-55% committed; second fund targets INR5,000 crores. Private credit fund targets INR1,500-2,500 crores. Public markets still loss-making due to AIF-to-SIF transition costs.

segments.name: Asset Services
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR245 crores (+53% YoY) on a low base; client assets INR1.63 lakh crores. Clearing yield moderated to about 2.5% in Q2 from normalisation of cash collateral in new clients.

segments.name: Capital Markets
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR175 crores (+9% YoY). ECM rebounded with IPOs above INR400 crores rising from 4 in Q1 to 38 in Q2; institutional broking hit by CAS impact of about INR2-3 crores per month in Aug-Sep.

guidance_outlook: Wealth and Private cost-to-income expected to improve 100-200 bps YoY this year and continue for at least two more years.
Full-year BAU opex about INR520-530 crores vs INR464 crores last year; with new BKC HO rent-free ROU charge of about INR25 crores, FY27 opex about INR550 crores.
ESAR scheme adds about INR20 crores per quarter to employee cost for next four quarters.
Clearing yield expected between 2.5% and 2.8% for next two years; full-year FY27 around 2.6-2.8%.
Client asset and focus-asset growth guided at 20-25%; Domestic custody business expected to grow about 20%.
Asset Management cost-to-income improvement expected after 12-15 months as new funds are deployed.
capex_capacity: Second commercial real estate fund to launch in about two weeks targeting INR5,000 crores; first fund about 50-55% committed.
Private credit fund (performing / special situations, 15-18% target return) to launch in 25-30 days, targeting INR1,500-2,500 crores over 8-10 months.
SIF launch expected in 25-30 days after approval received; private equity new fund planned for Q3 or Q4 or next year.
RTA for AIFs and PMSs to go live with minimum proposition by end-November or December; full scale by March. Trustee services between Q3 and Q4.
Added about 250 employees over 12 months (85-90% business-facing); about 90 RMs in Wealth and 14-15 RMs in Private added over the past year.
demand_pricing: Primary market activity jumped: IPOs above INR400 crores went from 4 in Q1 to 38 in Q2; pipeline of about 40 IB transactions (30 ECM, 9 advisory) with probability-adjusted revenue of INR85-90 crores.
ECM participation share about 15-18% of transactions; weaker in blocks, stronger in QIPs and IPOs.
Domestic PMS market share about 6-7% and AIF about 8-9% of book; capture about 25% of new domestic registrations.
Monetisation clients contributed about 35-38% of net new money over last 15 months.
Insurance is about 12-13% of Wealth revenue and zero in Private.
Competition: about 18-19 competitors in custody/clearing; new domestic custodian licences expected over the next two years.
Q2 cash volume down about 12% QoQ from CAS impact in secondary markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AMC one-time loss due to committed returns to investors?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It is unamortised upfront distribution cost on a venture fund pre-wound; for a INR1,000 crore fund with INR300 crore called, the INR700 crore balance is written off. Further INR8-10 crore accelerated amortisation over 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Anugrah-related surplus capital be released?
qa_highlights.answer: Excess capital was limited; a INR500 crore bank guarantee needed only about INR125-130 crore cash, which will be redeployed in clearing or other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Is the custody/clearing yield decline a threat from new domestic licences?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees about 18-19 competitors already; new licence holders are mostly asset managers. Clearing yield depends on cash vs G-sec mix (currently 38-40% cash) and is expected at 2.5-2.8% for two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt-to-equity restrict lending growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 2.5x from 2.9x; at 2.5x with about INR1,000-1,300 crore annual profit, around INR3,000-4,000 crore of incremental lending headroom is possible, so internal accruals may suffice. Dividend payout policy under board review.

qa_highlights.question: Clarification on PAG stake sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Nothing as of now; the process is being done by shareholders, and the company will disclose anything material.

risks_watch: Debt-to-equity at about 2.9x vs 2.5x target; rating and covenant pressure if leverage rises further; dividend policy to be reviewed with FY27 annual results (April 2027).
Asset Management cost burden from SIF, private credit and PE team build-up; cost-income improvement not expected for 12-15 months.
Clearing yield sensitivity to cash/G-sec mix and FPI collateral growth; competitive pressure from new custodian licences.
Q2 capital markets institutional broking hit by CAS; expected to reverse from December.
Wealth attrition: one team movement with about 75-80% arrested; no revenue impact expected.
Non-recurring items: INR9-10 crore amortisation over next 12 months and ESAR charge of INR20 crore per quarter for four quarters.
543988|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, flows and primary market recovery, while cautious on balance sheet and Asset Management cost. Management was candid that Q2 transaction income had a high base effect and that Q1 fixed-income gains will not recur.
key_quotes: Just to summarize, we delivered a reasonably good quarter of strong performance.
Client assets now are about INR5.5 lakh crores. Revenue was about INR937 crores. Operating PAT about INR319 crores, with a yearly growth of 26%.
If I take Q1 plus Q2 put together, we are about 11% to 12% of the opening balance, and our guidance has always been that we will be between 22% to 25%, which I think we are on track.
We will have to look at the dividends and maybe see whether we overall continue with that 40%-60% payout, because that can now become detrimental for shareholders.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides Wealth and Private cost-to-income to improve 100-200 bps YoY this year, but FY27 opex rises to about INR550 crore (BAU INR520-530 crore plus ~INR25 crore ROU charge) and ESAR adds about INR20 crore per quarter for four quarters, so the margin gain is conditional on revenue keeping pace.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Second CRE fund (INR5,000 crore target, first fund 50-55% committed), private credit fund (INR1,500-2,500 crore over 8-10 months), SIF and RTA go-live are all firmly scheduled within 1-2 quarters, and about 250 employees were added over 12 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Client asset and focus-asset growth guided at 20-25%, Q2 net new money about INR3,300 crore in Wealth and INR5,000 crore in Private, and client assets about INR5.5 lakh crore (+25%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed as such; new asset-management funds and the PE fund (planned Q3 to Q4 or next year) are the nearest equivalent, with debt-to-equity at 2.9x against a 2.5x target limiting balance-sheet-funded expansion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose 21% YoY and operating PAT 26%, but management flagged a high Q2 base, non-recurring Q1 fixed-income gains and CAS-hit institutional broking, so upside is conditional on IPO and ECM momentum (IPOs above INR400 crore rose from 4 to 38 QoQ).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Clearing yield is guided at 2.6-2.8% for FY27 against 2.5% in Q2, FY27 opex is raised to about INR550 crore, and debt-to-equity at 2.9x sits above the 2.5x target; Asset Management costs are not expected to improve for 12-15 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Private credit fund launch in 25-30 days, SIF launch in 25-30 days after approval, second CRE fund launch in about two weeks, and RTA go-live for AIFs and PMSs by end-November or December.

rows.label: Primary market / IPO pipeline recovery
rows.why: IPOs above INR400 crore rose from 4 in Q1 to 38 in Q2, and about 40 IB transactions with probability-adjusted revenue of INR85-90 crore are in the pipeline.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity back to 2.5x target
rows.why: Debt-to-equity is about 2.9x against a 2.5x target, and about INR1,000-1,300 crore of annual profit gives roughly INR3,000-4,000 crore of lending headroom, so internal accruals may suffice; the H1 FY27 dividend was skipped and policy is under review.

rows.label: Asset Management cost-to-income improvement
rows.why: Public markets are still loss-making on AIF-to-SIF transition costs, and an INR8-10 crore accelerated amortisation runs over the next 12 months, so the benefit only comes as new funds are deployed.

tone.note: Management was confident on flows, client assets and the primary-market recovery, and cautious on the 2.9x debt-to-equity, Asset Management cost burden and clearing-yield compression; analysts probed the AMC one-time charge, the leverage headroom and the PAG stake sale.

543989|2026-03.headline: Sai Silks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5.1% to ₹419 crore; FY26 revenue up 13.1% to ₹1,654 crore and PAT ₹141 crore.
543989|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 5.1% YoY to about ₹419 crore, with PAT of ₹32.65 crore versus ₹13.51 crore a year earlier, helped by a low base. Full-year FY26 revenue rose 13.1% to ₹1,654 crore with same-store sales growth of about 3%, and EBITDA margin expanded to 15.76%. Q4 EBITDA margin was about 14.6%, pressured by advertising timing, employee costs from late-quarter store openings, bonuses and Labour Code impact. Management guided FY27 net addition of about 1 lakh sq ft (at least 20% above FY26), SSSG similar to or slightly above 3%, and EBITDA margin of 17.5-18%.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹85 crore reported (about +65%); vs ~₹105 crore operational PAT in FY25

segments.name: Varamahalakshmi (VML)
segments.commentary: About 52% of FY26 sales per management; led growth in FY26 and is the highest-margin format, with high-single-digit SSSG in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

segments.name: Kalamandir
segments.commentary: Expected to lead FY27 expansion in Karnataka (Bangalore focus); FY27 format mix of roughly 60:40 Kalamandir to VML cited.

segments.name: KLM
segments.commentary: Sales declined about 3% in FY26; 9,000 sq ft capacity reduced in one store to improve margin; over 60% of KLM stores are in Telangana, weighing on state SSSG.

segments.name: State mix
segments.commentary: Telangana sales about ₹500 crore in FY26 versus ₹600 crore in FY23; Andhra Pradesh about ₹474 crore versus ₹443 crore; AP grew about 15% and Karnataka about 27%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 net retail addition about 1 lakh sq ft, at least 20% above FY26's ~78,600 sq ft gross addition; may be revised after H1.
FY27 SSSG similar to or slightly better than FY26's ~3%.
FY27 revenue growth expected above FY26's 13.1%; no numeric range given, to be clarified at end of H1.
FY27 EBITDA margin target of at least 17.5% to 18%; full-year EBITDA margin at least +50 bps expected per management.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1; April 2026 growth about low single digit positive.
No new borrowings planned in FY27; company is debt-free and expects no borrowing need for the next 2-3 years.
Advertising budget held at about 4% of sales, similar to FY26.
capex_capacity: FY26: 13 new stores and 1 extension added, taking network from 68 to 81 stores across 5 South Indian states; retail area about 785,000 sq ft.
FY26 gross addition about 78,600 sq ft; net addition about 69,000 sq ft after a 9,000 sq ft capacity reduction in Q4.

FY27 pipeline: about 1 lakh sq ft identified and closed; expansion mainly Karnataka (Kalamandir), with some VML stores in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu; at least one store outside core markets (Maharashtra) expected this year.
Store payback: VML within 8-9 months; maturity to company-average EBITDA margin in 1.5-2 years, longer for Kalamandir.
Inventory rose only ₹34 crore despite about 70,000 sq ft addition; inventory per sq ft down from about ₹11,533 to ₹10,480 since FY24; inventory days about 180 last year.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand softened in late January to February 2026 due to geopolitical and consumption factors; Q4 store openings (2 stores, 25,000 sq ft) came in March 10-15, contributing little revenue.
Tamil Nadu average revenue per sq ft about ₹32,300 for FY26; management expects 5-10% YoY improvement, with potential VML productivity gain of ₹4,000-5,000 per sq ft in Tamil Nadu.
Price increases over the last 6-7 months; average saree budget has moved from about ₹1 lakh to ₹60,000-70,000 per bill.
Gold price hikes expected to divert some spending toward sarees and apparel; management cited Adhik Maas slowdown in early Q1 FY27 until mid-June.
Wedding dates in FY27 expected 5-10% higher than FY26; Dussehra moved to Q3 from Q2 in FY27.
Gross margin protected via vendor discount improvements despite newer lower-margin formats.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 net square feet addition, SSSG and revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net addition about 1 lakh sq ft (at least 20% above FY26); SSSG similar to or slightly above FY26's ~3%; revenue growth to be firmed up at end of H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA margin fall to about 14.6% despite gross margin above 42%?
qa_highlights.answer: Advertising costs fell about ₹10 crore YoY but some spend landed in Q4; employee costs rose from stores opened Dec 15 to Mar 15, plus bonus (about ₹4 crore, roughly 2 bps) and Labour Code impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 growth slow, and is Valli contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied Valli mix as the cause; cited late-January to February consumption slowdown and late-March store openings.

qa_highlights.question: Format-wise sales split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined detailed split but said VML is about 52% of sales and growing as a share.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Telangana and Andhra underperforming?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly KLM, with over 60% of KLM stores in Telangana; VML SSSG in these states is high single digit; new stores are mostly outside Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Target 17.5-18% for FY27 versus about 16% in FY26, driven by VML mix and productivity gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why not expand faster given the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focused on maintaining productivity and margins, has closed about 1 lakh sq ft pipeline, and may exceed it after H1.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal target given; inventory per sq ft reduced to about ₹10,480; FY26 inventory days were about 180.

risks_watch: Q4 EBITDA margin of about 14.6% versus the FY27 17.5-18% target; execution on margin expansion.
Telangana and KLM underperformance and KLM's ~3% decline; plan to revive KLM SSSG not yet quantified.
Tamil Nadu flattening and Q4 sales decline; expected 5-10% productivity improvement is modest.
Depreciation sensitivity to AS 116 lease accounting as new leases are signed.
Entry into a new state (Maharashtra) could raise advertising and store-opening costs.
Inventory days remain high (about 180 last year); no target given.
543989|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the structural demand story and the FY27 store pipeline, but cautious and evasive on specific revenue, PAT and inventory numbers, deferring them to the H1 call. Management was defensive when questioned on the promoter and company tax demands and on the Q4 margin slide.
key_quotes: We still delivered strong double-digit revenue growth, significant profitability improvement, sustained margin expansion and also focused on our retail expansion.
One of the top high priority KPIs for us is to maintain the gross margin irrespective of the fact we are coming with the newer formats and lesser gross margin stores.
The challenge is not just opening retail stores and be okay with reduced margins.
The target would be the same. This year, we have reached about 16-point-odd.

543989|2026-06.headline: Sai Silks Q1 FY27 revenue flat at INR375 crore (vs INR379 crore) as SSSG fell 7.5–7.8%; FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12–15% retained.
543989|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR375 crore against INR379 crore a year earlier, with same-store sales degrowth of up to 7.5% (about 7.5–7.8% per Q&A). Management blamed Adhik Maas (May 17 to June 15), weak discretionary consumer sentiment and a high base (Q1 FY26 SSSG was double digit). EBITDA margin declined about 1% on fixed-cost deleverage, while gross margin held close to 42% (down 10–15 bps). Management retained full-year guidance of 12–15% revenue growth and an EBITDA margin better than FY26, and asked investors to judge the business annually rather than quarterly. Store count reached 83 with about 8,14,000 sq ft; one KLM Fashion Mall store in Telangana is being closed.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR379 crore in Q1 FY26, roughly flat
degrowth; Q1 FY26 base was double-digit SSSG
YoY, due to SSSG degrowth and fixed-cost deleverage
added about 30,000 sq ft in Q1; about 14 stores added over the year per analyst
vs INR61 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR53 crore in Q1 FY26; management attributed Q4 spike to bonuses and seasonal temporary staff

segments.name: Kalamandir (format)
segments.commentary: Majority of FY27 expansion; two new large Kalamandir stores (about 14,000 and 15,000 sq ft) opened in Karnataka in Q1, with brand strength cited as higher in Karnataka than Telangana.

segments.name: Varamahalakshmi (format)
segments.commentary: Co-lead format for FY27 expansion, with a pause in new Valli Silks stores of about 1–3 quarters due to higher rent-to-revenue (Valli stores 3,000–4,000 sq ft); next wave planned from Q4 FY27 or FY28.

segments.name: KLM Fashion Mall (Telangana)
segments.commentary: Sustained degrowth; one store being closed (store count 19 to 18), with inventory and staff to be moved to other KLM and upcoming stores. Innerwear reportedly growing and fashion jewellery only just being added; innerwear growth expected about 20% YoY.

segments.name: Telangana cluster
segments.commentary: Sharp decline of about 15% cited by analyst, linked to KLM; Dasara shift from Q2 to Q3 affects Telangana, a significant revenue contributor.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12–15% retained; management said it aims for around 15%, implying roughly 2–3% SSSG plus new-store revenue.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be better than FY26 closing; gross margin targeted to be maintained through the year despite cost pressures.

Net retail space addition target of about 1,00,000 sq ft for FY27; visibility of 26,000–30,000 sq ft in Q2 (total 58,000–60,000 sq ft after Q1 addition), 40,000 sq ft targeted for Q3–Q4, with possible extra 10,000–15,000 sq ft in Q4.
Entry into Pune (Maharashtra) and exploration of Kerala expected in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28.
Management indicated SSSG improvement of about 3–4% in the coming year as guidance basis, plus productivity from maturing and new stores.
Warehouse capex: deal for one location targeted by end-September 2026; full IPO fund utilisation targeted by September quarter 2026.
Wedding dates in Q2–Q4 expected to be 5–10% higher YoY; Sravana Masam from mid-August expected to lift demand.
capex_capacity: Added about 30,000 sq ft in Q1 FY27, taking store count to 83 and footprint to about 8,14,000 sq ft.

FY27 target of about 1,00,000 sq ft net addition, with management hinting at slightly more before year-end; total store-area addition in IPO plan was 1,42,500 sq ft, and about 90,000–1,00,000 sq ft extra was added within the same funds (about 80,000–90,000 sq ft per CFO).
Store split: Karnataka 14, Tamil Nadu 14, Telangana 28–29, Andhra Pradesh 28 (approximate, per CEO); Karnataka the lead growth market.
Warehouse: one of 1–2 identified locations under due diligence; deal targeted by end-September 2026.
Inventory per sq ft declining as cluster density improves; all stores company-owned, company-operated.
demand_pricing: Demand weak: value-conscious and discretionary purchasing; management attributes the Q1 weakness mainly to Adhik Maas, and also cites geopolitical factors, fuel and dyeing cost increases, and El Nino/poor rainfall in agrarian markets (AP, Telangana, Karnataka account for about 75% of revenue per analyst).
Post Adhik Maas (about 15–20 days after), demand slowly rising but below normal levels, per CEO.
Average ticket size about INR4,000–5,000; 95–96% of products sold at full price.
Management says it is the only listed ethnic wear player, so no direct peer comparison; jewellery growth of 35–40% cited by an analyst as a contrast.
Marketplaces (Amazon, Myntra) ruled out due to 20–45% commissions and high returns; e-commerce is a small channel.

qa_highlights.question: State-wise and format-wise split of the 1 lakh sq ft FY27 target, and any entry outside South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly existing territories, led by Karnataka; Kalamandir leads, with Varamahalakshmi also in play. New-state entry (Pune, Maharashtra; Kerala explored) expected in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Broadly unchanged; revenue growth guidance of 12–15% for the full year, with potential upside if stores open late Q3 or early Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company guide revenue growth and is rainfall a risk to demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 12–15% guidance and said agri-dependent cities (Rajahmundry, Vijayawada) are exposed; rainfall impact is expected to show in Q2–Q3 and is hard to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin outlook given supply chain cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin lost about 10–15 bps; the company aims to hold gross margin through year-end, with EBITDA margin better than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Telangana decline is from KLM, and what is the SSSG? Will KLM drag results?
qa_highlights.answer: SSSG about 7.5–7.8%, driven largely by KLM (mostly Telangana) plus the high base; one KLM store is being closed, with inventory and staff transferred.

qa_highlights.question: Wedding dates and Valli format performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2–Q4 has about 5–10% more wedding dates YoY, distributed evenly; Dasara shifts from Q2 to Q3. Valli operates at or slightly above Kalamandir productivity, but expansion is paused for 1–3 quarters due to high rent.

qa_highlights.question: Does the guidance imply flat or negative SSSG for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the 7% degrowth is a catch-up issue; the full year should balance, with about 15% growth implying around 2–3% positive SSSG.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue flat despite 14 new stores, and what is the demand trend in July?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher base and SSSG degrowth from Adhik Maas and lower consumption; demand improving post-Adhik Maas, with Sravana Masam from mid-August expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost drop from Q4 to Q1, and how is SSSG maturity measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 had bonuses and seasonal temporary staff; Q1 lower. SSSG maturity measured as the year of opening plus one year; FY27 guidance assumes 3–4% SSSG improvement plus maturing and new-store productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Warehouse funds unutilised since IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: One of 1–2 locations under due diligence; deal targeted by end-September 2026, with full fund utilisation expected in the September quarter 2026.

risks_watch: Sustained SSSG degrowth (-7.5% to -7.8% in Q1) with guidance relying on a recovery to about +2–3% SSSG in H2.
Rainfall, El Nino and agri-income exposure in AP, Telangana and Karnataka (about 75% of revenue per analyst), with impact expected in Q2–Q3.
Cost pressure from fuel, dyeing and supply chain, which could erode gross margin beyond the 10–15 bps already lost.
KLM Fashion Mall Telangana degrowth, with a second store under review.
Store addition pace: Q2 visibility of 26,000–30,000 sq ft; Q3–Q4 target of 40,000 sq ft, dependent on timing.
Valli Silks expansion paused 1–3 quarters due to high rent-to-revenue; warehouse capex still unallocated.

543992|2026-03.headline: Yatra FY26 revenue less service cost rose 24.5% to INR 4,824 mn and adjusted EBITDA 37.5% to INR 917 mn, but Q4 EBITDA fell 46% on MICE disruption.

Q4 was weak: revenue from operations fell 14% YoY to INR 1,890 mn and EBITDA fell 46% to INR 126 mn, driven by West Asia conflict cancellations and deferrals of MICE and international group bookings into FY27. Management said Q1 FY27 run rates are about 20% above Q4 and expects H2 FY27 to be materially stronger, while reiterating a medium-term 20% RLSC and 30% adjusted EBITDA CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the air discount rising and what is the take-rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said enterprise customers spend about 50% more per ticket than B2C, so airlines pay better realisation on enterprise. Net take rate is improving. Discount-to-gross-take was about 61% in FY23-24 and about 47-48% in FY25-26.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 tracking better than Q1 FY26, and is the 20% growth guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20-30 model is a 2-3 year CAGR view, not hard guidance. Q1 will be muted, with recovery expected in H2.

qa_highlights.answer: Discount as share of gross margin was about 75% last year and about 85% in FY26, driven by Q4. Management expects a return to about 75% or lower in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said organised MICE is about 10% of a roughly INR 35,000 crore market, and that Yatra is about the second-largest organised player. It cited exception handling and DMC partnerships as moats. MICE is 10-15% of installed base revenue.

qa_highlights.answer: Product expected within a quarter or two. Airline partnerships are needed to offset card fees, or the net take rate and numerator would suffer. Hotel virtual card is already live.

qa_highlights.question: Holding company (THCL) restructuring status?
qa_highlights.answer: The Cayman and Cyprus layer collapse is still in progress across India, Cyprus, Singapore and Cayman. THCL sold about 1.8% in Feb 26 to fund legal costs, and management does not expect further sales.

543992|2026-09.headline: Yatra Q2 FY27 revenue from operations fell 39% YoY to INR 2,136 mn, while gross margin held flat at INR 1,255 mn and net loss was INR 7 mn.
543992|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations fell 39% YoY to INR 2,136 mn, mainly on a sharp MICE decline (gross bookings down ~63% YoY) after an unusually strong prior-year quarter. Gross margin (revenue less service costs) was flat YoY at INR 1,255 mn, supported by air and standalone hotels, while adjusted EBITDA fell 41% to INR 150 mn and the company posted a net loss of INR 7 mn. Management said air gross bookings grew 15% YoY, air margin rose to 4.4% of bookings, and MICE grew ~37% QoQ. Other expenses rose on affiliate commissions, which management described as a short-term measure, and no formal annual guidance was given.

segments.commentary: Gross bookings down ~63% YoY against a very large prior-year international quarter, but up ~37% QoQ. Management accepted lower margins to retain large customers and rebuild volumes; Middle East exposure is ~35-40% of international travel and still muted ~15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has debt increased and how will it reduce?

543994|2026-09.headline: JSW Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore, but PAT fell 11% to INR328 crore on forex losses and Fujairah's nil contribution.

Logistics EBITDA more than tripled to INR81 crore, with the rail rake fleet raised to 78 from 42. PBT fell to INR431 crore from INR463 crore on unrealised forex losses and higher depreciation, and PAT fell to INR328 crore from INR369 crore. Management held the FY27 consolidated EBITDA target of INR2,950-3,000 crore, while revising logistics EBITDA margin guidance up to 28% from 24%.

543996|2026-06.headline: Updater Services Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR764 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR42 crore (5.5% margin) and PAT of INR30.3 crore.

Management declared an interim dividend of INR1 per share, about INR7 crore of cash outflow, and said it remains a net cash company. Management gave no formal guidance and pointed to Q1 as the indicator.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR161 crore, up 18% YoY, with EBITDA INR7 crore at 4.3% margin. Margin pressure came from a mix shift toward low-margin field marketing and budget timing at one large customer.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR28 crore with EBITDA INR5 crore, an 18% margin. Won 2 new clients that started in July on 2-year tenures, and started its first agentic AI engagement in May-June.

segments.name: BSS: Matrix (Audit & Assurance and EBGC)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 2% YoY and was flat QoQ. EBITDA rose about 76%, and margin improved to 13.1% from 7.6% (EBITDA INR4.2 crore vs INR2.4 crore). qa_highlights.question: Is the Matrix margin improvement sustainable, and has IFM margin moderation from headcount additions ended?
qa_highlights.answer: EBGC revenue went from INR11.4 crore (Q1 FY26) to INR11.7 crore (Q4 FY26) to INR12.5 crore (Q1 FY27), and gross margin from about 12% to 21%. Management says cost structure is flat, so volume drives margin, and it expects this to hold. IFM EBITDA was INR23.6 crore vs INR23.1 crore YoY, with some cost and contract front-loading.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash balance be used, and are buybacks planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is above INR300 crore across three buckets: inorganic growth, brownfield organic investment, and shareholder rewards. The INR1 interim dividend is the first step. There is no buyback proposal before the Board, though management did not rule one out.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IFM:BSS mix change over 2-3 years, and can agentic AI matter for Athena?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the 67:33 mix to hold, since both segments can grow 9-12%. Agentic AI is in use for outbound lead qualification and inbound repetitive queries. Management said it does not see wholesale replacement of human agents in BFSI near term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSS margin fall from 11.5% in Q4 to 7.5% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to a Q4 FY26 Avon restatement that added revenue to last year's Q4. Excluding it, Q4 BSS EBITDA was INR19.1 crore vs INR18.9 crore in Q1, so margins are similar.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the rise in other expenses and the tax-expense swing quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose because of restructuring costs and transport provisions taken in FY26. Tax fell on a manpower-linked tax benefit in a couple of group entities, and the mix is also a factor because Matrix gets no such benefit. Management said the full-year effective tax rate is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the SIS share purchases and the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no discussion with SIS beyond public knowledge; it reads the purchases as a treasury investment. The promoter family holds 59.1%. The acquisition is on hold over valuation.

543996|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to INR812 crore and EBITDA rose 37% to INR43 crore, with margin up to 5.3%.

IFM margin improved to 4.2% as large contracts moved past ramp-up and upfront employee costs normalised. BSS margin rose to 7.7% on 11% growth, with Denave's profit more than doubling, while Global (aviation) faced softer traffic and Athena and Matrix showed modest progress. Management declined formal guidance but suggested annualising H1 numbers, flagging headwinds in Denave and Global in H2.

544004|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 volume hit record 61.23 MMSCM (+12% YoY) and standalone EBITDA rose 77% to INR 47 crore, but management declined to guide Q3 margins.
544004|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue net of excise rose 29% YoY to INR 334 crore, with PAT more than doubling to INR 26 crore and PAT margin at 7.7%. EBITDA moderated sequentially from INR 62 crore in Q1 to INR 47 crore in Q2 because of higher gas sourcing costs and currency movement. A September HPHT allocation change by MoPNG temporarily cut gas availability for about a fortnight at the start of Q3, and management expects Q3 to be impacted, while still targeting roughly 15% EBITDA margin for H2. The company remains net debt-free with INR 45 crore of debt against INR 253 crore of cash and mutual funds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q3 raw material cost rise and what is the HPHT impact?

qa_highlights.question: Why will Q3 not be as strong sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Brent-linked billing with GAIL, Shell and IOC uses averaged pricing that spills into later quarters; Namakkal and Trichy depend on higher-cost IOC and BPCL/GAIL short-term allocations because GAIL pipeline projects are delayed.

Collections were about Rs 575 crore, and management said these fund construction without incremental debt on residential projects. Consolidated revenue was Rs 52 crore, EBITDA Rs 8 crore, PBT Rs 11 crore and PAT Rs 8 crore, with the P&L reflecting only a fraction of the contracted portfolio. ICRA assigned a first-time A+ (stable) issuer rating on a consolidated basis. Management declined to give FY27 sales guidance, though it did guide collections and deployment figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and marketing expense rise sharply YoY in Q1, and how should quarterly cost run-rate and EBITDA margins be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Nitin Kansal said Ind AS 115 recognises residential sales at possession while all advertising and marketing cost is expensed as incurred. Q1 had launches and ongoing sales effort versus no launches in the year-ago quarter, so costs look elevated. Future spend will track the launch schedule for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Which of Estate 361 Phase-2, Estate 105 Phase-2 and Sector 59 will be the biggest FY27 pre-sales contributor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to single out one project, saying the three are expected to contribute roughly equally, as they sit in different micro-markets (Dwarka Expressway, Golf Course Extension Road, Noida).

qa_highlights.question: How does the Antara arrangement work commercially, and what is the revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Sahil Vachani said Max India and Max Estates are separate listed companies. Estate 360 and 361 sit on Max Estates' balance sheet, with Antara as development manager at about 9.5% of topline on the Antara-branded portion. Nitin Kansal said senior living units sell at a 7-10% premium, and an Rs 5 crore senior living apartment would pay Rs 45-48 lakh as fee, collected over the project life.

qa_highlights.answer: Sahil Vachani narrowed collections guidance to Rs 2,500-2,700 crore, split equally between already-sold projects reaching construction milestones and fresh sales. Deployment on projects is Rs 1,500-1,800 crore, leaving OCF of Rs 750-1,000 crore for business development.

qa_highlights.answer: Sahil Vachani said guidance in the current volatile micro-economic environment is not good for long-term health, so the company will not give sales guidance. On Sector 59, the phasing decision will be taken closer to launch, though the entire project has approvals.

Sahil Vachani said the equity portion has been provided for, the long-term split is about 40% equity and the rest debt, and construction finance converts to lease rental discounting on commissioning.

544009|2026-03.headline: Blue Jet FY26 revenue fell 8% to INR947 crores on PI/API destocking, while Q4 contrast media revenue rose 91% YoY to INR193 crores.

544012|2026-03.headline: Cello World Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR654 crore (record quarter), but EBITDA margin fell to 20.9%; FY27 revenue guided at 10-12% growth.

Management attributed the soft Consumerware quarter to festive demand shifting into Q3 and to the steelware ramp-up, and said H1 and Q2 are not strictly comparable with last year. Cost pressure from the West Asia conflict, polymer, fuel and gas prices compressed margins, with glassware only breaking even. Management guided to about 10% revenue growth for FY27 and declined to give margin guidance.

Chinese glassware imports and freight costs, plus pending MIP outcome.

544014|2026-03.headline: Honasa Q4 FY26 revenue grew 28% YoY to INR682 crore with EBITDA at 11.3% (~2.5x YoY) and PAT of INR69 crore.

544014|2026-06.headline: Honasa Q1 FY27: revenue grew 32% with EBITDA near INR110 crore and PAT INR90 crore; management says FY27 growth will beat the high-teens five-year CAGR.

Management attributed margin expansion to B2B mix, A&P efficiency, opex leverage (about 100 bps) and a non-recurring one-time opex benefit, and said the one-time item was not recurring. Focus categories grew 35%+ and reached about 85% of sales; Mamaearth accelerated to high-teens growth and the second INR1,000 crore brand (The Derma Co.) was announced. Management also disclosed the entry into fragrances (FIKN) and the Fluence Pharma acquisition under Honasa Health, still pending conditions precedent.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion is organic versus seasonal, and does seasonality reverse from Q2?

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the company about no repeat of past distributor inventory build-up?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier Mamaearth fragrance extension was shut down because consumer PMF was poor; it argued fragrance needs to be a fragrance-first brand, and built internal R&D over about two years before launching FIKN.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA guidance too conservative given Q2 seasonality and H2 patterns?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 ex one-time was about 12% margin; Q2 scale dips sequentially and the company remains growth-first, reinvesting where needed; margin target remains 100-150 bps a year over four to five years.

544023|2026-09.headline: Kalyani Cast-Tech guides FY27 order book rising to ~INR170 crore from INR133 crore, with H1 expected to lag and H2 to catch up.
544023|2026-09.overview: Management presented FY26 results showing revenue up about 7.7%, PAT up about 20% and EPS up about 20% year on year. The company cited an order book of about INR133 crore, of which roughly 50% is innovative containers and INR45 crore is from government customers, and said it expects this to reach about INR170 crore soon. H1 FY27 was described as not going to plan due to war-related supply chain disruption, with management saying H2 would catch up. Capacity additions included a second Shivlakha (Kutch, Gujarat) container line, a rail-connected Gati Shakti cargo terminal, ICD permission and a wagon plant awaiting RDSO audit.

financial_highlights.value: None drawn; INR100 crore HDFC Bank sanction available

segments.name: Container manufacturing (Rewari, Haryana)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~7,000 TEU, FY26 output ~5,400 TEU, utilisation ~75-80%. Management guides container PAT margin ~10-11%.

segments.name: Container manufacturing (Shivlakha, Kutch)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~10,000 TEU per year, production started June 2026 with 500 containers delivered; plant has surplus capacity. Overall capacity cited as ~17,000 TEU.

segments.name: Wagon manufacturing
segments.commentary: Phase-one capacity 2,400 wagons per year; factory complete but awaiting RDSO G-105 audit. Design stage-1 cleared; 60-70% of wagon cost is bought-out items, so value addition is limited.

segments.name: ICD and rail terminal
segments.commentary: ICD permission received 10 Sept 2026, warehouse foundation laid 14 Sept, operations expected by next financial year. Management guides EBITDA margin ~25-30% for ICD and terminal operations.

H1 FY27 expected to be weaker than planned due to supply chain disruption from war; management expects H2 catch-up but gave no H1 figure.

Container capacity to be expanded from ~17,000 to ~25,000 TEU to qualify for the INR10,000 crore government container scheme; guidelines still awaited.

Land of ~144 acres (possibly 150) at Kutch; ~60 acres kept for a large factory with offtake partner.
Capex funded from internal accruals and promoter warrants so far; management says debt and preferential issue/rights issue are under consideration for the next expansion.
demand_pricing: Order book ~INR133 crore, about 50% innovative containers (dwarf open-top, stainless steel, foldable, wide 20-ft with roof hatches, super high-cube 40-ft, two-wheeler triple-deck) and 50% standard containers.

Customers cited include JSW Ports (~1,500 containers this year), Western Carrier (50 foldable containers), Central Warehousing Corporation and Indian Navy (new, ~INR30 crore orders), Container Corporation via business associates, Pristine Logistics, Amba Coach Builders, Rail Connect and HTPL.
Pricing not disclosed; management declined to give average price of innovative containers.
Management said India's domestic container market is cyclical and that China supplies ~95-97% of global containers; the company claims ~60% share of Indian domestic container manufacturing.
Briskworld Ventures receivable of ~INR4.67 crore (per annual report) is now being paid, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the new Kutch facility add to FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated the INR170 crore figure, which it described as the order book target, and did not give a separate top-line number.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company benefit from the INR10,000 crore container manufacturing scheme, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidelines are awaited (2-4 months expected). Company would need 25,000 TEU capacity to qualify as brownfield; currently ~17,000 TEU.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company have enough capital and what are the EBIT/PAT margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion to ~20,000 TEU more needs significant capex; options are bank debt (HDFC INR100 crore sanction), preferential issue or rights issue. Container PAT margin ~10-11%; ICD/terminal EBITDA ~25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: When will the RDSO wagon approval come and what is the stage-2 timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage-2 documentation to be submitted in 1-2 weeks; then prototype and oscillation trials. Final approval targeted by 31 March 2027. G-105 is a separate factory audit still pending; no inspection expected before Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any MOU, patent or equity interest from customers?
qa_highlights.answer: The MOU is with RDSO for joint design development. Management said the design is company-controlled. No customer or institution has shown interest in equity; management said it may not pursue such tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for a new foundry and when?
qa_highlights.answer: New foundry (INR80-90 crore) to come in the next financial year, after wagon orders are confirmed. A small corner-casting foundry exists at Rewari.

544027|2026-03.headline: Fedbank Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40% YoY to INR100.5 crore, with AUM at INR20,153 crore (+27%) and gold AUM up 76%.
544027|2026-03.overview: Fedbank crossed INR100 crore quarterly PAT for the first time, with ROA of 2.6% and ROE of 14%. Growth was led by gold loans, where disbursals hit INR10,744 crore in Q4 and gold AUM reached INR10,352 crore. Asset quality improved sequentially, with GNPA at 1.9% (from 2.1% in Q3) and credit cost at 0.7% in Q4 and 0.8% for FY26. CRAR rose to 22.4% after a INR450 crore subordinated debt raise and secured-book sales, despite leverage rising to 4.6x.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gold yields soften in the last two quarters, and is origination yield under pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 5-10 bps to deliberate pricing and the rest to back-ended disbursals. Origination pressure is seasonal, and Q1 should recover; competition has not yet entered the company's catchments.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new LTV and margin rules raise NPAs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a margin breach does not require provisioning or NPA classification; only margin calls are triggered. About 90% of the book is below 75% LTV.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ST LAP business profitable and will it grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to say if the INR3,800 crore book is currently profitable, and said it expects a better answer in about a year. ST LAP growth is expected to track the market, with internal issues described as resolved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 ROA and credit cost path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets ROA up 20-30 bps over FY26 in FY27, through opex or credit cost, with a similar path in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Gold AUM per branch and peer comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: Average AUM per branch is INR16.2-16.5 crore overall; branches open before FY25 average about INR20 crore. Capacity is INR60-65 crore per branch.

qa_highlights.question: How is April 2026 for asset quality and collections?

Gold loan AUM grew 77% YoY to ₹11,191 Cr despite a roughly 15% fall in domestic gold prices and new RBI LTV rules effective April 1. Stage II rose from 2.2% to 2.7% due to the shift to periodic interest-due structures, which management attributes to customer re-adjustment rather than asset quality. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20-25% entity growth, 20-30 bps ROA expansion and sub-1% credit cost, and announced leadership changes in the LAP and gold businesses.

544027|2026-09.headline: Fedbank Q2 FY27: PAT rose 63% YoY to INR130.8 crore and ROA hit a record 2.8%, but GNPA rose to 1.8% on gold-loan repayment-model transition.
544027|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter on profitability: PAT of INR130.8 crore (up 14.3% QoQ, 63% YoY), ROA of 2.8% and ROE of 17%, both records. AUM grew 37% YoY to INR22,035 crore, with gold AUM up 77% YoY to INR11,917 crore. Management attributed the rise in GNPA (1.6% to 1.8%) and Stage II (2.7% to 3.6%) mainly to the shift from bullet to periodic interest-due gold loans, which it called technical. Management flagged intense gold-loan competition in Q2 and said it would keep growing and guiding for Q3 and Q4.

Opex as a share of average total assets was 4.9% in Q2 vs 4.8% in Q1 and 5.5% in FY26, reflecting full-quarter branch and headcount costs.
AUM per gold branch rose from INR8 crore to INR16 crore (cited in the Q&A); management said cost-to-income should fall as AUM per branch grows.
demand_pricing: Gold-loan competition was heightened in Q2 across geographies, with NBFCs using yield, LTV and lending-practice strategies. Gold yield fell about 10 bps over Q1 and Q2 combined, per management. Management said bank competition is in a different yield segment.

Gold LTV is 68% overall; customers take the maximum LTV available (75-80% in most cases), and the portfolio has a mix of 71-74%. Income-generating loans (about 20% of disbursements) are priced on cash flow with LTV caps of 75-85%.
ST LAP origination yield has fallen from 16.1% to 14.9% over 5-6 quarters; management attributed this to state mix and competition, not ticket size, and said yields should improve in Q3.
Approval rates in ST LAP have recovered to mid-40% from about 30% after BRE tightening.
Medium-ticket LAP is partner-driven, runs at 11.5-12.5% yield, and is a steady, profitable business.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage gold loan growth and yields given rising competition from NBFCs and banks? Is an income-generating loan product ready?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 competition was the most intense yet, and it chose a balance of growth and yield. Gold yield fell only about 10 bps across Q1 and Q2. The IGL product has been live since April, with LTV structured at 75-85% based on cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Stage II and III rises in gold: is this the new normal, and will it deteriorate further in Q3-Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Stage II rise technical, since most gold loans are 2.5-3 month tenor products and customers are moving to periodic interest. It said the change could take 1-2 more quarters to settle, and it declined to give a Stage II number. CFO said there have been no auction losses in six years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ST LAP yields fall, and how much will they rise with rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall mainly to state mix, not ticket size, and said Q3 yields will be higher than Q2 with higher disbursements. ST LAP ticket sizes have moved up to INR7-8 lakh, with a minimum of INR8 lakh now.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 AUM and ROE guidance be raised given H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept AUM growth guidance at 20-25% for FY27 and said ROE could see upside. Target is ROA 3% and ROE about 18%. Management said upside depends on gold prices.

qa_highlights.question: How will rate hikes affect spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said pass-through will be limited, with the company absorbing part of the shock. Offsets will come from opex and credit cost. Fixed-rate borrowings are 33%, MCLR-linked 24%, and about 58% of the loan book is short-tenor gold loans that reprice at maturity.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the mortgage business and its ROA as mix shifts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold ROA will be maintained, not expanded, as AUM per branch rises and cost-to-income falls. ST LAP ROA is expected to move toward gold ROA over time, and the gold mix will not drop in the next cycle.

544030|2026-09.headline: Flair Q2 FY27 revenue rose 6.5% QoQ to INR340.1 crore, EBITDA margin fell to 14.9%, and FY27 growth guidance was cut to 12%+ after Valsad/Daman floods.
544030|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR340.1 crore, up 6.5% QoQ, with exports up 13% QoQ to INR49 crore and domestic sales up 6% QoQ to INR292 crore. Floods in Gujarat shut the Valsad and Daman plants for about 15 and 7 days, costing an estimated INR25 crore of revenue. EBITDA was INR50.6 crore (14.9% margin) and PAT rose 9.1% QoQ to INR31.7 crore (9.3% margin). Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance at 12%+ and said FY28 onward growth should be about 15%, while flagging higher raw material costs from West Asia and a rise in working capital days to 145.

segments.commentary: Grew 24% YoY in H1 FY27. Q2 was hit by Valsad disruption, and a new Creative facility is planned in Valsad.

qa_highlights.question: Was the FY27 growth guidance cut from 15% to 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the guidance is 12% for FY27, which it said was already set on the last call, and about 15% from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why were pens less affected by the floods than steel bottles and Creative?
qa_highlights.answer: Pens were supported by other plants in Uttarakhand, Mumbai outskirts and Daman. Steel bottles are made at Valsad, which was down about 15 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth needed in H2 and how will it be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to H2 FY26 growth of 17-18%, Creative and steel bottle push, and the Q4 fourth line. It declined to give October numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating leverage or raw material pass-through drive margins as growth accelerates?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said margins are planned at around 15% with a buffer for volatility, and could rise if raw material prices give a benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating margin fall more than gross margin QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said flood-related costs could not be spread across production in Q2, which is temporary and should reverse in coming quarters. No one-time items were included in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Export receivable days rose due to global disruption; domestic receivables were not rising. Target is to cut working capital by about 20 days over 5-6 quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is open to a partner with a strong manufacturing base; the brand stays with Flair. No size or timing was disclosed.

544044|2026-03.headline: India Shelter Q4FY26: AUM up 29% YoY to Rs 11,044 crore, PAT Rs 138 crore (+27% YoY), ROE 17.6%, Stage-3 down to 1.2%.
544044|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 showed strong YoY earnings growth, with PAT of Rs 138 crore (+27% YoY, +11% QoQ) and ROE of 17.6%. Asset quality improved, with 30+ DPD down 100 bps QoQ to 4%, gross Stage-3 at 1.2% and net Stage-3 at 0.9%. Management guided to a more cautious 25-30% AUM growth for the next three years, with disbursement growth of about 20% in FY27, citing the macro environment (LPG disruption, geopolitical stress). Management framed a Rs 30,000 crore AUM target by 2030 as achievable at 27-28% CAGR.

544044|2026-06.headline: India Shelter Q1 FY27: PAT up 23% YoY to INR 143 crore and ROE 17.5%, but Stage 3 rose to 1.5% and reported AUM growth slowed to 24%.
544044|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR 143 crore (23% YoY, 4% QoQ) with ROE of 17.5% and net worth of INR 3,353 crore. Gross AUM reached INR 11,284 crore, up 24% YoY, after a one-time switch to recognising disbursements on cheque realisation rather than handover, which cut reported disbursements to INR 641 crore. Stage 3 rose to 1.5% (up 30 bps) on seasonal and early-bucket delinquency, and management guided Stage 3 to stabilise in Q2 and recover from Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for 25-30% AUM growth, 40-50 bps credit cost, more than 6% spreads and 40-45 branch additions, though analysts questioned the credit trend and the disbursement ask rate.

Stage 3 expected to stay around the Q1 level (about 1.5%) in Q2 and fall from Q3 as SARFAESI actions take effect; 30+ DPD expected to decline from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% AUM growth guidance still achievable given the cheque-realisation disbursement change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change is one-time and disbursement growth above 20% is still expected, supported by July's INR 400 crore; AUM growth of 25-30% is retained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 3 and 30+ DPD rise, and is it company-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality and stress in the self-employed, sub-INR 7 lakh ticket cohort (above 2% Stage 3 versus 1.4-1.45% three years ago), and to the cohort's 16%+ yields. It said there was nothing internal, and that April collections were 96.2-96.4% and June slightly above 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company hold credit cost at 50 bps with Stage 2+3 at multi-year highs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of holding 50 bps, citing low LGD on this cohort and management overlays. Stage 3 is expected to stay flat in Q2, with recovery from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no branch addition in Q1 and why is disbursement growth only about 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said branch openings are phased by strategy, with most of FY27's 40-45 coming from Q2. It said peers' Q1 numbers were on a different base and that the full-year target is what matters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is incremental yield up 30 bps while incremental cost of funds is stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bankers are asking 20-25 bps higher cost of funds, with the overall impact limited to about 10 bps, so the company is passing on some cost to new disbursements. Incremental yield is 14.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the gap in the Q1 FY26 AUM base?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is about INR 450 crore of co-lending book, which was not previously included in AUM. From March 2026 it is included, so the correct YoY AUM growth is 24%.

544045|2026-09.headline: DOMS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17.6% to INR667.8 crore, but EBITDA margin held at 12.4% as raw material inflation (~15%) outpaced pricing.
544045|2026-09.overview: Operating revenue grew 17.6% YoY to INR667.8 crore in Q2 FY27 and 18.4% in H1, with over 80% of growth from volume. EBITDA was INR82.8 crore in Q2 and INR165.3 crore in H1, both at a 12.4% margin, with the quarter held sequentially flat despite a sharp raw material rebound from August. Flooding in Gujarat cut sales growth by an estimated 300-350 bps and caused a one-time INR10.4 crore exceptional loss, for which insurance claims have been filed. Management chose a patient, measured pricing stance, deferring a more aggressive margin-recovery push by a couple of quarters, and guided consolidated sales growth of 18-20% for the year.

financial_highlights.change: margin 5.7%; includes INR10.4 crore one-time flood exceptional loss
EBITDA margin 6.4% vs 8.1% a year ago

segments.name: Scholastic stationery, art and office supplies
segments.commentary: Broad-based growth on capacity added over the last year; office supplies and adhesives named as main growth drivers. Kits and combos grew only marginally due to capacity constraints.

segments.name: Hobby and craft (adhesives)
segments.commentary: Strong momentum from an expanded adhesive range and added capacity; management expects it to be a key growth driver.

segments.name: Back-to-school
segments.commentary: Strong growth led by the recently launched pencil box range; compass and school box range is early but gaining traction.

segments.name: Hygiene / Uniclan (baby diapers, wet wipes)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 21.5% with both volume and price; EBITDA margin fell to 6.4% from 8.1% on raw material costs. Long-term target 8-10%.

segments.name: Reynolds writing instruments
segments.commentary: Production started in the first 50-acre building (~170,000 sq ft) for Brite and 045, with Jetter click pen in trial. Revenue expected from Q3 FY27, gaining momentum in Q4; MRP kept unchanged.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth guided at 18-20% for FY27, reiterated despite the flood impact.

Long-term EBITDA margin target of 16-17%; management says it will be patient for a couple of quarters before deciding on significant pricing action. Pre-West Asia conflict consolidated margin was close to 17%.
Capex of INR100-125 crore expected in H2 FY27 after over INR200 crore in H1.
Debt of about INR100-120 crore needed in the midterm to fund capex; internal accruals expected to fund more once margins normalise.

Reynolds business plan expected to be clearer by next quarter; management said a one-year timeline for reaching the INR150 crore pre-acquisition writing instrument revenue would be cut to nine months.
Detailed FY28 outlook deferred to January-February discussion.
capex_capacity: First building of 50-acre greenfield facility commissioned (~170,000 sq ft) for office supplies and Reynolds pens; second and third buildings have machinery being installed; three more buildings at finishing stage.
Planned additions in the new facility: wooden pencil manufacturing and further office supplies capacity before FY27 close; pen tip manufacturing being installed for backward integration.
H1 FY27 capex over INR200 crore, mainly for the 50-acre site, land adjacent (footprint raised from 45 to 50 acres), machinery and Reynolds asset purchase.
Uniclan added one baby diaper line and one wet wipes line; spare capacity remains, so no further capex planned until FY28-29 review.
Seven SpA JV: DOMS Seven Private Limited incorporated in October as a wholly owned vehicle; Seven SpA to take 50% stake once documents (apostille) and JV agreement are finalised.
demand_pricing: Volume contributed over 80% of the ~18% revenue growth; realisation about 20%.
Raw material inflation was about 15% after early-quarter cooling; price increases were taken selectively at SKU level, with schemes and discounts reduced versus last year.
Price increases took 3-4 months to reach the market because of MRP-based pricing and about two months of printed packing inventory.
Raw material prices rose from early-to-mid August and kept increasing through October, with price changes happening once or twice a week.
Net consumption impact is about 9% of costs, versus about 10% in Q1.
Regional: West slowed due to lower merchant exports to Bangladesh after geopolitical disruption; management says consumption is evenly spread across four regions.
Reynolds fixed overheads (team integration) cost about 0.5-1% of sales in Q2, a temporary margin drag.

qa_highlights.question: Split of growth between volume and realisation, and how much raw material inflation has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% of the ~18% growth was volume and about 20% realisation. Pricing is calibrated and lags the market, with management describing it as a catch-up game.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realistic margin outlook and why not pass through faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged near-term margin pressure. The 16-17% target stands, but it will wait a couple of quarters before deciding on more significant action, and says this is not a commitment to a specific quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Reynolds integrated, and why relocate its manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales and support teams are fully integrated under the field force, with some distributor rightsizing. Moulds and assembly machines were moved from Chennai to Umbergaon because the Chennai infrastructure was not part of the deal. Pricing is unchanged for now.

qa_highlights.question: Why not start the new plant with pencils, given less raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Pens were always the priority given market opportunity. Machine lead times of six to eight months were ordered before the conflict. Management says the timing difference is about one quarter at most.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt is being added and what is the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt has roughly doubled from March to about INR200 crore, funding capex, Reynolds and working capital. Management expects it to need INR100-120 crore more in the midterm.

qa_highlights.question: How long does the industry take to pass through inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: At DOMS, full capture of an inflation cycle has taken about 18-24 months from the start, and the company has already spent two quarters in it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the raw material basket up 15% versus 10% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Inflation is about 15%. The 10% figure in Q1 was the impact on consumption, now about 9%, an improvement of about 2 points.

risks_watch: Raw material costs still rising into October and linked to West Asia conflict and crude; no margin visibility guided.
Margin recovery to 16-17% depends on pricing actions that are deferred by a couple of quarters; a further squeeze is possible if costs keep rising.
Reynolds ramp-up: revenue expected only from Q3 FY27, and the margin drag from integrated staff costs needs to normalise.
Rising debt and working capital needs (about INR100-120 crore more in the midterm) while free cash flow is weaker.
Flood-related disruption and the INR10.4 crore loss; insurance recovery timing is not fixed.
Bangladesh export disruption affecting West region sales.
544045|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on volume and capacity, but cautious and evasive on margins: management repeatedly said visibility is limited and chose to be patient rather than commit to a margin recovery timeline. Deferred FY28 and detailed Reynolds questions to later calls.
key_quotes: So it's like a catch-up game that we are playing, and we will take calibrated actions wherever we believe that there is possibility to increase the prices.
We follow a very simple mantra nothing at the cost of market and at the same time, nothing at the cost of margin.
But what we've seen at DOMS is about 18 to 24 months. That is the outer limit from the start of the cycle.

rows.why: First 50-acre building (~170,000 sq ft) is commissioned, second and third buildings have machinery being installed, and Reynolds revenue starts Q3 FY27 with wooden pencil and office supplies capacity before FY27 close.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume was over 80% of the ~18% H1 growth, and FY27 sales growth of 18-20% is reiterated, backed by new capacity and the Reynolds ramp, though no order book was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: INR100-125 crore of capex is firmly planned for H2 FY27 after over INR200 crore in H1, with INR100-120 crore of midterm debt needed to fund it, and Seven SpA JV incorporated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 sales growth guidance of 18-20% was only reiterated despite the flood hit of an estimated 300-350 bps, and no margin guidance was raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material costs were still rising through October with no margin visibility, and the flood cut growth by an estimated 300-350 bps, so further squeeze is possible.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Reynolds Brite, 045 and Jetter click pen revenue is expected from Q3 FY27 and gaining momentum in Q4, with the compass and school box range still gaining traction.

rows.label: Catch-up pricing to lag raw material inflation
rows.why: Price increases lag by 3-4 months and management says pricing is a catch-up game, with a deferred decision on significant action (raw material inflation ~15%, realisation ~20%).

rows.label: Seven SpA JV 50% stake
rows.why: DOMS Seven Private Limited incorporated in October; Seven SpA takes 50% once apostille and JV agreement are finalised, with no date given.

rows.label: Reynolds overhead drag normalising
rows.why: Reynolds fixed overheads cost about 0.5-1% of sales in Q2 as a temporary drag, and management expects it to normalise as the business integrates.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume, capacity and the 18-20% sales guide, but cautious and evasive on margins, deferring the 16-17% recovery timeline by a couple of quarters; analysts pushed on pass-through of inflation, the timing of Reynolds and debt build-up.

544046|2026-03.headline: INOX India Q4 FY26 total income rose 24.2% YoY to INR475 crores; FY26 revenue INR1,632 crores (+21.2%) with 23.8% adjusted EBITDA margin and INR1,514 crore order book.
544046|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, export revenue and order booking in Q4 FY26, with total income of INR475 crores and adjusted EBITDA of INR108 crores (+13.4% YoY). Full-year adjusted PAT was INR261 crores (+19.3%) and adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.8%, which management said was in line with or better than guidance. Key wins included a roughly INR200 crore US aerospace order, a INR85 crore Cochin Shipyard marine LNG tank order, and a repeat ITER order. Working capital and operating cash flow weakened as project-based, milestone-billed orders grew, with contract assets rising and operating cash flow of INR116 crores in FY26 versus INR177 crores in FY23.

financial_highlights.change: Up from INR731 crores in FY25 (per analyst)
Lower than FY25 per analyst; INR177 crores in FY23 (per analyst)

segments.name: Industrial Gas Solutions

segments.name: LNG Solutions
segments.commentary: Entered marine LNG with Cochin Shipyard order for 6 x 800 cbm LNG fuel tanks (~INR85 crores, 2-3 year delivery). Management cited ~INR122 crores run-rate for LNG per analyst question; 60% export and 40% domestic. Bahamas mini LNG order: ~INR240 crores total, ~INR160 crores supplied in FY26, balance in FY27.

segments.name: Cryo-Scientific
segments.commentary: Repeat ITER order for cryostat panel modifications; LOX tank for submarine application completed. Management expects ~INR50-60 crores per year of ITER work over at least 5 years; a third ISRO launchpad tender is expected by end of the quarter.

segments.commentary: Keg dispatches up 31% to ~61,000 units (FY25 ~46,000); segment revenue ~INR26.13 crores vs ~INR27.15 crores in FY25 due to mix shift to 20-litre kegs. Approvals/orders from Heineken, AB InBev and Molson Coors; installed capacity ~300,000 kegs/year, utilisation about one-third.

At least INR1,200 crores of the INR1,514 crore order book expected to execute in FY27.

Management expects LNG division to grow faster than standard products, citing 15-20% cost advantage of LNG versus diesel/petrol.
capex_capacity: Kandla facility under development on ~7 acres near Kandla Port; commissioning in ~9-10 months, targeting LNG mega storage tanks and large aerospace tanks.

Global beverage keg market ~120 million kegs, 4-5 million replacement demand per year; INOX is second in Asia.
US disposable refrigerant cylinder demand is constrained by refrigerant gas producer quotas; growth expected to be marginal, with share gains targeted from other US customers.

Project orders now above 60% of order book versus ~30% earlier, with standard tanks declining as a share.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects more orders of similar size in Q1 or Q2 FY27 and targets INR450-500 crores of order booking per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline in Q4 and what is the Cochin Shipyard order value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed quarterly variation to product mix, with the annual margin in its 21-24% band (23.8% in FY26). The Cochin order is ~INR85 crores for six 800 cbm tanks, to be delivered over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why has operating cash flow lagged sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said milestone-based payment terms on project orders (10-90% stages) push cash receipts behind POCM revenue recognition, raising contract assets; advances of ~INR500 crores partly offset this. Management said project orders are over 60% of the book, so limited OCF growth is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Highview Power opportunity and INOX's share?
qa_highlights.answer: INOX currently supplies only cryogenic liquid air storage tanks for the first project, which is small by value; management expects future projects to be 8-10x larger in order value, with a further project in ~6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue shares of kegs and disposable cylinders, and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Keg revenue was ~INR26.13 crores in FY26 vs ~INR27.15 crores in FY25; disposable cylinders were ~INR150 crores in FY26 vs ~INR135 crores in FY25, with an RFQ expected within a month and ordering in the next fiscal year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the MSRTC bus conversion order and the data-centre cooling tie-up?
qa_highlights.answer: MSRTC buses are running but the customer is not pushed due to payment issues and reportedly now works with others. Data-centre cooling is an R&D-stage MoU with a European partner; a 6-12 month development timeline was given, with INOX offering the full cryogenic cooling solution.

risks_watch: Working capital and operating cash flow: contract assets rising with project-based milestone billing; FY26 OCF INR116 crores.
Logistics and supply chain constraints, plus the West Asia conflict affecting Middle East shipments and LNG supply, were flagged as ongoing headwinds.
US tariff pressure on disposable cylinder and transport exports; US refrigerant cylinder market flat due to producer quotas.
Lumpy LNG orders; management said LNG order timing can vary quarter-to-quarter.
LNG truck adoption faced near-term challenges per management; import competition from Chinese LNG tanks is limited by PESO approvals per management.
Pipeline conversion items to monitor: Q1/Q2 FY27 aerospace orders, ISRO third launchpad tender, Starbucks coffee keg trial orders, Highview follow-on projects, Kandla commissioning.

544046|2026-06.headline: INOX India Q1 FY27 order inflow hit a record ~INR532 crore, lifting order book to ~INR1,686 crore; revenue of INR382 crore grew ~8.3% YoY, below management's own INR410-415 crore target.
544046|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 total income was INR382 crore (+8.3% YoY) and EBITDA INR90 crore (+1.4% YoY, 23.5% margin), with PAT flat at INR61 crore. Management attributed the revenue shortfall to INR32-35 crore of equipment ready for dispatch but held back due to freight rate spikes and ship availability issues. Order inflow was a record ~INR532 crore, driven by a large US space-sector cryogenic tank order, with the order book at INR1,686 crore, of which over INR1,140 crore is export. Management reiterated 18-20% FY27 revenue growth guidance and a 21-24% EBITDA margin range.

segments.name: Industrial Gas Solutions
segments.commentary: Won 8 large 1,500 cubic metre cryogenic storage tanks for a global space exploration customer plus 6 repeat tanks; also disposable cylinder repeat orders (crossed 2 million cylinders in FY26) and Cryoseal/liquid cylinder traction with capacity expansion. Semiconductor orders from Dholera were modest (~INR30 crore+ per management in Q&A).

segments.name: LNG Solutions
segments.commentary: Orders from Sabarmati Gas, Ultra Gas and BPCL for LNG fuelling stations and healthy LNG semi-trailer orders. Bahamas mini LNG terminal: first large tanks reached site, installation underway; two more orders for Eleuthera and Great Abaco. Cochin Shipyard marine LNG fuel tank execution continues.

segments.name: Cryo-Scientific Division
segments.commentary: Secured a CERN order for specialised cryogenic modules and another order from ITER France. Management said big LNG and CSD projects are delayed by customer issues and regulatory approvals, expected to materialise in one to two quarters.

segments.name: Beverage Kegs
segments.commentary: Orders from Heineken India, Hartwall Finland, ORBEN Germany and a UK brewery; RFQs from Asahi and CCU Chile. Keg capacity is 300,000 units and is under-utilised; management guides utilisation from ~30% to 50-60% by year-end.

segments.commentary: Received AS9100D certification, enabling onboard flight components beyond ground support equipment. Overall US private space order exposure is over INR1,000 crore; management said about INR400 crore of the current order book is aerospace.

544055|2026-09.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q2 FY27: record Rs 2,900 cr disbursement, PAT Rs 110.8 cr standalone, average cost of borrowing cut to 9.93%.

Credit cost was 2.6%, within the 2.5-3% guided range, and GNPA improved 32 bps QoQ to about 3.38%. Average cost of borrowing fell from 10.13% to 9.93%, the first time below 10% in company history. Management flagged the El Nino-linked drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka as a watch item, with about 3.6% of on-book portfolio (around Rs 550 crore) exposed and most of it covered by NATCAT insurance. FY27 guidance was reaffirmed.

544057|2026-03.headline: Happy Forgings Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20.4% YoY to Rs.424 crore, with EBITDA margin at 31.5% and FY27 volume growth guided to late-teens.
