544057|2026-06.headline: Happy Forgings Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% to Rs.449 crore and PAT 39.2% to Rs.91 crore, with EBITDA margin at 31.3%.
544057|2026-06.overview: Record quarterly revenue and profit, driven by 23.1% volume growth and 3.2% higher realisations to Rs.253/kg. EBITDA rose 39.3% to Rs.141 crore, margin up about 275 bps YoY, the fourth straight quarter above 30%. Management says customer price revisions are partly in Q1 (about 30%) and will fully reflect from Q2. Exports were hit by transit delays, with the domestic CV business up about 18%.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles
segments.commentary: 33% of revenue; single-digit growth overall (about 7% per analyst math). Domestic up about 18%; exports down about 12% due to DDP shipments delayed about a month by geopolitical transit issues. CV export share about 7% of revenue.

segments.name: Farm equipment
segments.commentary: 32% of revenue; grew mid-20s. Domestic up over 20%; exports grew despite weak US and Europe tractor demand. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: 16% of revenue; around 50% growth in both domestic and export. Export share about 9% of revenue. Drivers cited: power generation, wind, railways, oil and gas, digital infrastructure.

segments.name: Off-highway
segments.commentary: 11% of revenue; over 40% growth in both domestic and export. Domestic construction equipment up about 9%. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: About 8% of revenue; growth over 70%, domestic over 40%, exports more than doubled as earlier-secured orders began executing. Export share about 8% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth trajectory hold across industrial, export and PV, and can the high gross and EBITDA margins sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to strength across CV, farm, PV; a ~Rs.950 crore order book; and new high-realisation products. It said the last price increase was three years ago, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price-revision benefit flow from Q2, and is it permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% came in Q1. Domestic: 2% taken in Q1 versus 4.5-5% total, with OEMs passing on from Q2. Increases are on a three-year-old base and described as permanent; currency gains supported exports.

qa_highlights.question: Will solar benefit come in Q4 FY27 and can margins stay above 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar expected on stream from January, with some generation in Q4 and connection through April. Management is confident of upwards of 30% EBITDA margin, citing a 1-1.5% power benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CV revenue grow only ~7% against ~10% industry production growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic CV grew ~18% against ~10% production growth; exports fell ~12% because DDP contracts (Europe, Turkey) saw about a month of deliveries delayed by transit issues.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight cost impact and recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Container costs rose from about USD 2,000 to USD 6,000. About 75% of contracts are pass-through; company expects a 15-20% hit and is negotiating recovery of about USD 4,500 per container.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export mix by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate export share of revenue: CV ~7%, PV ~8%, farm ~5%, off-highway ~5%, industrial ~9%.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the Rs.950 crore order book and the Rs.650 crore capex, and plant-level margins for the new industrial line?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book roughly 35-40% industrial, 25-30% PV, 25-30% CV, rest off-highway/farm; 60% export, 40% domestic. New heavy-line gross margins expected around 60-65% with EBITDA about 50% of gross; plant-level margins not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: receivable and inventory days as of June 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days improved with no big change; inventory days about 50 as of date; overall working-capital days improved.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 guidance be revised given strong Q1 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is high-teen volume growth and it should perform better than that, without giving a revised number.

qa_highlights.question: Asset turns and high base in PV and CV as capex comes on stream in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not worried about a temporary six-month to one-year dip in asset turns, since capacity is being built for future growth; PV growth is from two to three customers with customer acquisition ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic plans and funding of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Open to acquisitions and JVs, mainly for technology in energy and aerospace; cautious on expensive valuations in farm/CV. Growth to be funded largely by internal accruals, possibly with a one-year bridge loan for LCs.

544057|2026-09.headline: Happy Forgings Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32.7% YoY to Rs.501 crore and PAT grew 32.8% to Rs.98 crore; Rs.500 crore new capex approved.
544057|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached Rs.501 crore (+32.7% YoY) on 24.8% volume growth and 6.3% higher realisations to Rs.267/kg. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs.950 crore (+29.9%), with PAT up 35.8% to Rs.189 crore and PAT margin of 19.9%. Management approved an additional Rs.500 crore capex, mainly machining, phased across FY28-FY29, on top of the Rs.650 crore heavy-component programme that is now guided to commission in Q4 FY28. Management reiterated that full-year margins may be similar to FY26, citing raw material pass-through and higher export freight costs.

segments.name: Farm equipment

Includes about Rs.300 crore hammer line (fungible, 300 kg to 3 t), Rs.200-250 crore dedicated machining lines, and Rs.150 crore vertical upsetter line for wind and North American farm equipment.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book and pipeline is export-linked, and how is the new Rs.500 crore capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 50% of the order book is export, with over Rs.95 crore of recent Asia export orders. The Rs.500 crore capex is 70% machining and 30% small press forging lines, with land already acquired.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 4,000-ton press line built for a North American PV customer, and what revenue will it generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it serves a North American PV client and ramped up in Q1-Q2. Sales are largely DAP and in transit, recognised from Q3. Management projects about Rs.80-100 crore of sales from this facility.

qa_highlights.question: Has the heavy-line commissioning timeline changed from Q4 to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No change: equipment arrived in FY27, full forging trials are planned for Q4 FY27, and sample submissions and revenue begin in FY28 Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any risk to data-centre capex given US election concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no issue: the customer has already invested, the market is short of heavy-forging capacity, and even Rs.1,000 crore of orders is about 5% of the total market.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins moderate to FY26 levels given strong H1, and is it due to pass-through or cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA per kg has improved despite cost pressures and should be maintained in H2. Raw materials are fully passed through; the solar plant adds about 1.5% to EBITDA from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt will fund the new Rs.500 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management proposes Rs.300 crore of bank debt as a bridge, need-based and possibly partly utilised, with the rest from internal accruals and cash over 1.5-2 years.

544058|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR162 crore with EBITDA flat at INR42 crore; management guides FY27 to flat store count and mid-single-digit same-store growth at best.
544058|2026-03.overview: Credo Brands (Mufti) reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 6% YoY to INR162 crore, with gross margin of 58.8% and EBITDA flat at INR42 crore (25.6% margin) as advertising was stepped up to about 8% of revenue. FY26 revenue was flat at INR592 crore, with EBITDA of INR154 crore (26% margin). The company closed 24 stores and opened 7 in the quarter, reducing the network by 17. Management said FY27 is a consolidation year with roughly 20 openings and 20 closures, with ad spend rising to 8-10% of revenue and margins likely lower.

544088|2026-03.headline: Medi Assist FY26: total income up 23.6% to INR923.2 crore, operating EBITDA margin 19.3%, company turned debt-free in Jan 2026.

544088|2026-06.headline: Medi Assist Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 24.1% YoY to INR236.5 crore, with operating EBITDA margin at 20.3% and retention down to 90.2%.

544095|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 591 crore, down about 8% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 25.8 crore (down about 64% YoY) and a 4.37% margin versus 11.21%. Net profit was Rs 2.4 lakh after a Rs 32.42 crore reversal of PLI income accrued in the first nine months and Rs 21.78 crore of RIPS 2024 incentive recognised in the quarter. For FY26, revenue was Rs 1,894 crore (down 12.7%), EBITDA Rs 113.9 crore (down 27.7%), margin 6.01%, and net profit Rs 3.3 crore. Management said early FY27 trends look better, with industry growth of about 15% expected in Q1 and a strong order book.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the PLI benefit reversed and what were the eligibility conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the criteria were investment in the prior year and 5x incremental revenue growth for applicable components; capex was met but incremental revenue shortfall led to reversal of Rs 32.42 crore, pending auditor review and government clarification. The total FY26 eligibility was about Rs 56.5 crore, with only about Rs 32 crore accrued before Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off net effect on profit (around Rs 11-12 crore per an analyst)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is larger: the Rs 32.42 crore reversal plus Rs 24 crore of unrecognised Q4 PLI, leaving a difference of about Rs 35-36 crore versus the full eligibility, after Rs 21 crore of RIPS was booked.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the sharp rise in inventory and payables days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the working-capital build to summer-season inventory, imported compressors stocked ahead of a BIS expiry in mid-April, and payables rising in step; inventory was about Rs 800-837 crore at end-March and management expects normalisation by quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue double in two to three years and will EPACK outgrow the industry in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the Rs 5,000 crore ambition in two to three years and said EPACK should outgrow the roughly 15% industry growth, but gave no numeric guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken and will margins compress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cumulative price increases of 15-20% were taken by end-March, with a further rise in April and May; some lag is expected in Q1, with a Y-o-Y margin squeeze but some sequential improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RAC utilisation level in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annualised utilisation fell to roughly 20-40% (figures given inconsistently) from 45-50% historically; peak-season utilisation fell to about 75% from about 90%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Hisense JV exposed to China-related policy risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPACK funded the Sri City facility itself under a tech-transfer arrangement, sees no policy impact, and expects Hisense to expand into washing machines and other products in Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the auditor qualification about?
qa_highlights.answer: The qualification relates to a Rs 19.61 crore receivable from customer Gangnam, which is sub judice; management said it believes the amount is recoverable and has filed legal complaints.

544095|2026-06.headline: EPACK Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR886 crore (+34% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 6.21% from 8.24% as PLI income dropped to nil.
544095|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose about 34% YoY to INR886 crore, the company's highest quarterly revenue, with RAC up about 44% (roughly 30% volume, 14% value). EBITDA was INR55 crore, up about 0.7% YoY, with margin at 6.21% versus 8.24%; management said the prior-year figure included INR13.31 crore of PLI income, and the like-for-like underlying margin was about 6.4% in Q1 FY26. Net profit was INR11.8 crore, and management cited a forex loss of about INR6-7 crore and higher wage costs as pressures. Management said FY27 is the last year of PLI benefit and is rolling back PLI discounts shared with brand customers, aiming to fully reverse them by year-end.

Target utilisation of all three plants (Dehradun, Bhiwadi, Sri City) at 55-60% for FY27 average; management said more than 60% on average.

Capex: total budget ~INR450-470 crore; ~INR330-350 crore booked; INR60-70 crore additional capex expected in the remaining nine months; depreciation not expected to rise significantly over next three quarters.
Hisense: cumulative expected revenue of ~INR8,000 crore over five years; management said on track for calendar 2026 and front-load washing machine production by end-October.
Andhra Pradesh MoU: INR1,085 crore investment over five years, ~35 acres allotted; state investment subsidy about 50% of capex over 10 years.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR10 crore; ~INR60 crore in CWIP expected to capitalise over the next two quarters.

FY26 utilisation: Dehradun and Bhiwadi ~55%, Sri City below 25%.
Washing machine and LDA capacity ramp flagged as fastest-growing; front-load washing machine pilot to mass production around end-Oct 2026.

Compressors: management said domestic compressor capacity installed and in pipeline (operational by end-December) is sufficient; imports allowed until end of calendar 2026. No plan for in-house compressor capacity in the near term.
demand_pricing: RAC: channel inventory considered largely liquidated after old-BEE-rated stock sell-through allowed until end-June 2026; management estimates industry inventory at 3.5-4 million units, the lowest acceptable level.

Pricing: contracts with large customers reset prices quarterly; most commodity pass-through completed with a time lag, and management said little price increase remains to be passed on. Forex was the main margin headwind.

Customer base: 72 customers and 19 product categories at FY26 close; ~73 customers and 19 product lines now, targeting ~75 customers and 20 product lines by end-FY27. Three new categories added in Q1, four more in pipeline.
Commodities: no forward hedging; back-to-back booking against confirmed orders, with changes passed through in the following quarter.
Inventory: in-house inventory mix roughly 70-75% AC and 25-30% non-AC; working capital days ~50-60, with inventory elevated due to BIS/QCO revisions.

qa_highlights.question: Top 2-3 execution priorities and biggest risks (demand, regulation, competition)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to AC tailwinds continuing and faster growth in SDA/LDA (washing machines) and components, with more customers added across categories. No specific risk list was given beyond the outlook commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the ~44% RAC growth between volume and value, and whether the volume growth is anchor-customer driven?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% volume and about 14% value (AOP increases and commodity pass-through). Management confirmed the volume growth is largely from the anchor customer.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost escalation is still to be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts reset prices quarterly and the prior quarter's increase was already passed on; little remains. The main margin hit was forex, which produced a loss of about INR6-7 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory levels and working capital trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry inventory estimated at 3.5-4 million units, the lowest acceptable level. Working capital days are about 50-60, with in-house inventory still slightly elevated due to BIS/QCO revisions; the company aims to normalise it.

qa_highlights.question: Compressor supply risk as BIS/QCO relief expires around March 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports allowed until end of calendar 2026, with domestic capacity installed and in pipeline (operational by end-December) judged sufficient. No plan for in-house compressor capacity in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for depreciation, finance cost and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation not expected to rise significantly over the next three quarters. Finance cost rose about INR3-4 crore QoQ on ~40% growth, with scope to reduce via inventory normalisation. Total capex budget ~INR450-470 crore, with ~INR330-350 crore booked and INR60-70 crore more over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue and EBITDA margin outlook; PLI impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal revenue guidance; industry AC growth ~20% expected and EPACK to outgrow it. Ex-PLI EBITDA ~6.5% in recent quarters; PLI worth roughly 1-2% of margin, shared ~50:50 with customers. Management is rolling back PLI discounts with the aim of full reversal by year-end, with normalised EBITDA from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Sri City utilisation, operating leverage and FY27 utilisation target?
qa_highlights.answer: Sri City reached close to 50% in Q1 FY27 (from under 25%), while Dehradun and Bhiwadi ran above 85%. Management targets 55-60% average across the three plants for FY27, and said it is above 60% on average.

qa_highlights.question: Hisense progress and washing machine timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60,000 ACs delivered Jan-Jun season for ~INR120 crore revenue; Q1 alone ~35,000 units for ~INR65 crore. Front-load washing machine pilot underway, mass production targeted by end-October. Management said the five-year ~INR8,000 crore plan is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity hedging policy, especially copper?
qa_highlights.answer: No forward booking in anticipation of orders; back-to-back booking against confirmed orders, with changes passed through in the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 PAT positivity and structural seasonality fix, and the INR5,000 crore FY29 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 and Q3 have historically been loss-making; the company targets stopping this in 4-6 quarters and declined to guide on Q2 FY27 PAT. Top-load washing machines are in production for three national/multinational brands; management said it is largely on track for the FY29 INR5,000 crore target.

qa_highlights.question: Components revenue decline of about 23% and SDA/LDA margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the 23% figure but said components will keep growing; current components are AC-linked (controllers, cross-flow fans, copper tubing). SDA/LDA gross margin is about 1.5-2 percentage points above AC (the transcript says 'basis points'). Non-AC components are being explored.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the spike in other expenses (>50%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a forex loss of INR6-7 crore, plus higher wage costs from the 35%+ rise in sales and production value.

qa_highlights.answer: Largely yes, with an ongoing lag as escalations pass through in subsequent quarters, and most vendors have had increases passed on.

qa_highlights.question: Post-PLI margin outlook and need for further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins to improve as PLI discounts given to brands are rolled back in phases and mix shifts to SDA and LDA; no numerical margin guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Hisense sales figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately INR90 crores in H1; about 18,000 ACs sourced this year to September.

qa_highlights.question: Debt, finance cost and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt about INR770-775 crores, similar to last year; total finance cost flat despite revenue doubling; debt/equity about 0.8x in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: Is any margin pass-through still left and what is the utilisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Some lag remains, but no significant gap; utilisation to improve with Hisense, washing machines and new southern customers; no explicit earnings guidance.

risks_watch: Forex volatility (INR/USD and INR/CNY) and commodity price swings, with pass-through lagging by a quarter.

Hisense washing machine ramp from December 2026 and whether the 18,000 AC run-rate translates into sustained volume.

544105|2026-03.headline: Harshdeep Hortico H2 FY26 revenue rose to INR 36.1 crore-range with EBITDA of INR 11.3 crore, but FY26 revenue of INR 69 crore missed the INR 85 crore internal expectation.
544105|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 H1 revenue of about INR 32.64 crore and H2 of about INR 36.1 crore, versus INR 24.9 crore and INR 31.51 crore in FY25. EBITDA rose to INR 8.4 crore in H1 and INR 11.3 crore in H2 (from INR 5.95 crore and INR 9.0 crore), and PAT to INR 5.7 crore and INR 6.82 crore. The CFO said full-year revenue of INR 69 crore fell short of the INR 85 crore expectation because of LPG gas cuts of about two months, raw material (PP) prices up 20-25% or more, and deferred luxury orders. Management said demand is holding flat year-on-year but not growing, and that margins are being defended by passing on only part of the cost increase.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 24.90 crore in H1 FY25 (about +31%)
vs INR 31.51 crore in H2 FY25 (about +15%)
vs internal expectation of INR 85 crore; FY27 guidance cited as INR 115 crore
vs INR 5.95 crore in H1 FY25
vs INR 9.0 crore in H2 FY25; EBITDA margin about 31% vs about 28% in H2 FY25
vs INR 4.22 crore in H1 FY25
vs INR 5.47 crore in H2 FY25
affected by geopolitical issues this year

segments.name: Roto moulded series
segments.commentary: About 30.66% of FY26 revenue per management; described as the highest-quality, high-volume, high-margin category with about 10-year warranty. Management said this segment was hit hardest by the price-driven slowdown.

segments.name: Grower series (injection moulded nursery pots)
segments.commentary: Described as about 30-40% of revenue and 42-43% of margins; high volume, low margin, about 1 lakh pots per day. Management said demand is not materially affected, with about 10-15% growth in the segment.

segments.name: Decorative series
segments.commentary: About 14% of revenue; affected by deferred purchases alongside roto moulded products.

segments.name: AgriShield shade nets
segments.commentary: Introduced in FY26; about 3% of revenue. Management guided to roughly 10-20% growth and said capacity at 100% efficiency, with the Pune line fully booked.

segments.name: Fiberglass, EcoSeries, garden furniture and fountains
segments.commentary: Fiberglass about 3.78%, EcoSeries about 1-2%, garden furniture about 1%. Roto moulded fountains launched in March 2026 with a 10-year warranty, and management reported 15-20 days of order backlog.

segments.name: Channel mix
segments.commentary: B2B about 75% and B2C about 25% per one answer; later a B2C ballpark of 15-18% of current revenue excluding wholesaler sales. Management said 13 major distributors and seven showrooms, mainly for wholesalers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance of INR 115 crore was referenced by an analyst; management did not confirm a firm number and avoided giving one.
Management said 25-30% annual growth is achievable if geopolitical conditions normalise.
Management said the current infrastructure can support revenue above INR 100 crore, and claimed comfort with 35-40% growth from existing capacity.
Management said it will hold margins as far as possible and expects to pass on only part of the cost increase.
Next detailed commentary expected after H1 FY27 results; no formal con-call scheduled before then.
capex_capacity: Three factories: Bhiwandi (about 1 lakh sq ft, largest), Pune (about 40,000 sq ft) and Delhi (about 20,000-25,000 sq ft, newly added this year).
Two warehouses (Bhiwandi and Bangalore), with an added Pune warehouse and a Kolkata warehouse serving the Northeast.
About 10% of facility capacity affected by raw material and LPG shortages, per management.
Solar panels installed on the Pune factory; management expects savings of about INR 10-15 lakh per month, MW capacity not disclosed.
No FY27 capex plans announced; management said it is comfortable and would discuss any future capex.
demand_pricing: Raw material (PP) prices up about 60% per management, from INR 100-120/kg to INR 160-170 (some grades INR 220); company passed on about 20-25% in wholesale prices, with competitors at 25-30%.
Customers are holding back orders; management said April-May sales are flat year-on-year with no decline and no exponential growth.
Current order book: three airport orders (Lucknow, Mumbai, Visakhapatnam) worth about INR 1.5 crore, plus ongoing showroom orders.
Ugaoo is the largest customer, at about 10% of business, up from about INR 1 crore to about INR 10 crore this year.
Export share about 2% of revenue; new export markets in Canada, USA and the Netherlands this year.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix between B2B and B2C, and whether B2B is order-book driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B is about 75% and B2C about 25%, with pots purely B2B and garden furniture and fountains sold B2C. Current order book was about INR 1.5 crore of airport orders.

qa_highlights.question: Realistic FY27 revenue and three-year growth aspiration after the FY26 shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a firm number, citing LPG cuts, labour shortage, raw material spikes and deferred projects. It said 25-30% annual growth is realistic if conditions normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold around 30% after raw material inflation, and has price been raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices were raised about 20-25% on wholesale rates (not MRP), with the company holding back on full pass-through to avoid losing customers. Management said it will keep margins as high as possible.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rising YoY, and what is the sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to inventory build for capacity growth and sudden orders (e.g., about INR 1 crore in two weeks for an event), plus credit to large customers and new stores. It gave no target number.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory (up 62%) and receivables (up 51%) growth due to pre-stocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no pre-stocking; it held stock for only 15-20 working days during raw material shortages and expects the condition to be temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 EBITDA margin about 31% vs about 28% last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality, with H2 driven by festivals and landscaping projects and higher-margin roto moulded and decorative products, plus the new fountain launch.

qa_highlights.question: How are large B2B and infra orders won, and what is the margin differential versus distributors?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders come through landscapers and subcontractors who tender on the company's behalf, as payment security is needed. Management said distributor and project margins are the same, with discounts of 45-50% based on order value, and the project margin is about 17%.

544107|2026-09.headline: BLS E-Services Q2 FY27 total income rose 55% YoY to INR 428 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44% to INR 29 crore, helped by the Atyati acquisition.
544107|2026-09.overview: Management reported a record quarterly total income of INR 428 crore for Q2 FY27, up 55% YoY, with operating EBITDA of INR 29 crore (6.8% margin). Profit after tax rose 12% to INR 21 crore, which lagged revenue growth. Growth was attributed to broad-based gains across businesses and the Atyati Technologies acquisition, completed on 2 July 2026. Management said the business is asset-light and debt-free, and that it expects H1 momentum to continue into H2.

segments.name: Business Correspondent (BC) services
segments.commentary: Largest segment, acting as banking outlet for partner banks (account opening, deposits, withdrawals, remittances, pensions, benefit payments). Q2 FY27 BC gross transaction value was over INR 41,400 crore vs INR 27,300 crore in Q2 FY26.

segments.name: Loan disbursement (Aadifidelis and BC network)
segments.commentary: Sources and processes loans for banks and NBFCs. Management calls it an important growth engine; no segment-level figures were disclosed. Co-origination for micro and agri loans is being developed.

segments.name: E-governance
segments.commentary: Citizen services for state governments (Aadhaar enrolment, land records, utility bill collection, welfare schemes). Offers over 330 services; won West Bengal mandate for Ayushman Bharat beneficiary verification earlier in 2026. No segment figures disclosed.

segments.name: Assisted e-services (BLS Seva)
segments.commentary: Merchants offer over 700 services including insurance, bill payments, railway bookings, telemedicine and education. No segment figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the momentum of the first half to continue into H2 FY27.
Management said it remains confident of delivering sustained profitable growth in FY27 and beyond. No numeric guidance was given.

Priorities: complete Atyati integration, raise productivity, grow revenue per touchpoint, scale loan distribution, expand e-governance into Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand, and pursue disciplined acquisitions.
capex_capacity: Total touchpoints over 1,88,200 as on 30 September 2026, up from over 1,47,000 a year earlier.
BC network and customer service points over 74,400, up from over 45,400 a year earlier.
Bank tie-ups for BC business, including loan disbursement, rose to 192 from 144 in Q2 FY26.
Asset-light, merchant-led model: local entrepreneurs fund premises and equipment, which management says allows expansion without large capex.
Ongoing investment in cloud-ready platform, AI tools for reconciliation and agent support, and cybersecurity. No capex figure was disclosed.
demand_pricing: Public sector banks are seeking loan leads from the company; private banks want help expanding into new geographies.
Received empanelment mandates from Punjab and Sind Bank and Chhattisgarh Grameen Bank.
Management said rural and semi-urban credit demand is strong.
Revenue comes from transaction commissions, loan distribution income, registration and renewal fees, and multi-year government contracts. Management said no single stream dominates.
Sequentially, revenue and operating EBITDA each grew close to 40% over Q1 FY27 as Atyati integration contributed.
risks_watch: Profit after tax grew only 12% in Q2 and 9% in H1 against 55% and 40% revenue growth, so margin and cost conversion need tracking.
Atyati integration is still in progress; management wants to lift productivity and standardise processes across the larger network.
Acquisition-driven growth: part of the Q2 jump came from Atyati (completed 2 July 2026), so organic growth is not separately disclosed.
Segment-level revenue and profit were not disclosed, so the contribution of each business is unclear.
EBITDA including other income grew 23% in Q2 and 16% in H1, slower than operating EBITDA.

key_quotes: We expect the momentum of the first half to continue and remain confident of delivering sustained profitable growth in FY27 and beyond.
This is the highest quarterly total income in the company's history.
Our asset-light model helps us grow quickly while keeping the balance sheet debt-free.

rows.why: Named as a priority with no timeline or capex, and it is only a planned expansion so far.

544111|2026-03.headline: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12% to INR 707 crore, with PAT of INR 66 crore; Q4 revenue up 4% to INR 184 crore.
544111|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR 184 crore (up 4% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 53 crore (28.85% margin) and PAT of INR 12 crore (6.44% margin). Management blamed Q4 cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad on the Middle East war, saying occupancy there has recovered to over 90%. For FY26, revenue grew 12%, EBITDA was INR 218 crore (30.82% margin) and PAT was INR 66 crore (9.21% margin), with profitability hit by the Middle East war and higher depreciation and finance costs. Management reiterated the plan to double hotels to 85 and keys to 6,635 over four years, and said the EM Bypass Kolkata apartment sales are ahead of plan on cash flow.

financial_highlights.change: resilient despite high base; YoY not stated
ARR up 9% YoY; RevPAR up 7% YoY

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Park Calcutta ran at 100% occupancy for Q4 and FY26; Park Chennai (95%) and Park Navi Mumbai (93%) were the other top-three occupancies. Delhi and Hyderabad saw large Q4 cancellations, now recovered to over 90% occupancy.

segments.name: Flurys (F&B retail)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 29% YoY and the brand has 110 outlets. Management said it is profitable but did not share segment EBITDA. Plans to add 30+ outlets in 10 months (NCR 8, Pune 5, Bangalore 4).

segments.name: F&B overall
segments.commentary: F&B revenue crossed INR 300 crore in FY26, about 43% of total revenue.

segments.name: Real estate (EM Bypass Kolkata)
segments.commentary: 29 of 34 apartments sold in the first block at an average INR 20,857 per sq ft. Cash flow improved by over INR 11 crore up to April 2026, with a further ~INR 70 crore expected this year; second block launch planned for Sep-Oct 2026.

guidance_outlook: Reach over 3,000 keys by FY27 after adding 12 hotels (472 keys), of which 8 are asset-light.
Over four years: hotels from 42 to 85, keys from 2,677 to 6,635; owned hotels to double, asset-light to triple.
Flurys to reach 140 outlets (or slightly more) after 30 additions in 10 months, and 40-50 more outlets by 2030.
Park Mumbai Juhu (78 rooms) construction to start June 2026, completion by about March 2027.
Malabar House (Cochin) acquisition expected to close in June 2026; Vizag (100 rooms) moved to early 2030 opening due to environmental clearance delays.
Interest cost at about 8.35% (MCLR), expected to stay below that level; capex and acquisition needs of about INR 1,500 crore over five years, mainly funded by internal accruals.
Management said earlier mid-teens top-line growth guidance was missed; FY26 came in at 12%.
capex_capacity: Five projects (Pune, Mumbai, Vizag, EM Bypass, Jaipur) totalling 950 rooms at about INR 1.2 crore per room, about INR 1,100 crore before the EM Bypass reduction.
EM Bypass expected to contribute INR 350 crore, of which INR 70 crore is expected this year.
Zillion and THALI acquisition/project cost about INR 330 crore; normal capex about INR 40 crore per year; Flurys capex about INR 30-40 crore per year.
Q4 FY26 launches: Zone by the Park Darjeeling, Zone Connect by the Park Gangtok and Zone Connect by the Park Katra; 7 properties (283 keys) launched in FY26.
Flurys moving from central kitchen to an outsourced manufacturing vendor (agreement signed).
Room renovations planned at Chennai, Bangalore, Kolkata and Vizag; 20 rooms at Park Calcutta to be refurbished.
demand_pricing: Management cited limited branded supply in India (about 216,000 rooms) and said supply growth is 200-300 bps below demand growth.
Kolkata has 5,101 keys with about 1,702 keys expected over five years; management said the outlook is positive, helped by the change of state government.

Ran Baas The Palace (Patiala, leased) ran at ARR of about INR 31,000 in FY26; Lotus Palace Chettinad at about INR 12,000 ARR and about 30% occupancy; Patiala targets about 50% occupancy in the Oct-Dec season.
Cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad in Q4 due to the Middle East war; management said contracts with ministries and corporates have been re-established.
Park Calcutta has about 30% repeat customers and T-RevPAR near INR 24,000, which management said is above luxury peers in its CBD.
Management said the Operation Sindoor disruption hit Q1 FY26 and the Middle East war hit from late February into April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ADR decline sequentially and grow only 3% YoY in Q4, and why was FY26 growth 12% against a mid-teens expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 weakness to large cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad from the Middle East war, which have since stabilised. It said 12% growth was good given two disruptions (Operation Sindoor in Q1 and the Middle East war).

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Flurys outlet count below earlier guidance, and what is the achievable expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan is 30+ outlets in the next 10 months (from 110 to about 140), largely cafes, with flagships in each new market; 40-50 more outlets by 2030. Management said the asset-light model with outsourced production allows faster rollout.

qa_highlights.question: How is 100% occupancy at Park Calcutta calculated when the website shows rooms available?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 100% means all rooms occupied every day, that the hotel has delivered near-100% occupancy for about 10 years (excluding COVID), and that its revenue management and repeat base (about 30%) drive this.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata outlook and how is the EM Bypass sales progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kolkata supply is limited and the state government change is positive. Apartments were launched at about INR 18,225 per sq ft and are now selling near INR 21,000; second block expected around the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: How will Flurys maintain quality with the central kitchen dropped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the central kitchen plan was dropped in favour of an outsourced vendor, with recipe standardisation, quality checks and quality chefs on site at the production facility.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company keep interest costs under control during the capex cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Atul Khosla said the interest rate is about 8.35% (MCLR) and will stay below that. Capex of about INR 1,500 crore over five years is mostly funded by internal accruals, with about INR 80 crore cash on hand; project interest will be capitalised as IDC.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the Vizag delay to 2030 and the status of Malabar House?
qa_highlights.answer: Vizag was delayed by environmental clearance, which is now in place; the project has no basement, so it may be faster, but management kept a 2030 timeline. Malabar House acquisition is expected to close in June 2026 after bank approval for foreign payment.

Geopolitical and LPG supply disruption, and its effect on costs and travel demand.

Vizag delay to 2030 and dependence on government permissions for new projects.

544118|2026-03.headline: Jana SFB met all Q4 FY26 guidance: PAT INR140 crore, net credit cost 0.47%, SMA 3.66%; FY27 guided to PAT growth of 80%+.
544118|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered on every guidance point set in Q3: PAT of INR140 crore (guided INR140-160 crore), net credit cost of 0.47% (INR156 crore) against 0.79% in Q3, and SMA of 3.66% versus a guided ceiling of below 4%. Gross slippages of about INR334 crore were the lowest in roughly eight quarters, and management said the MFI stress is behind it. Advances grew 23% YoY to INR36,289 crore and deposits grew 23% to INR35,784 crore, with cost of funds down to 7.46%. FY27 guidance calls for gross loan growth of 19-21%, deposit growth of 23-25% and PAT growth of 80%+.

segments.commentary: Grew 76% YoY; 2-wheelers offered in 135 cities and used cars in 50 cities; Q3 expected to be strongest on Diwali demand.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Up 81% YoY but only 0.3% QoQ; 65-70% of the Jan-Mar 2026 6-month loans came up for renewal in Q2. Management expects growth of about 10% a quarter from Q3.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: Growth slowed to about 3% (management expects 7-8% at best); no loosening of credit criteria.

segments.name: Microfinance (MFI)
segments.commentary: Now 26% of gross loan book; collections at 99% including BC book; growth subdued given weak bureau histories among borrowers. 97% of customers have two or fewer MFI lenders vs 93% industry.

segments.name: Unsecured advances
segments.commentary: Up 17% YoY but down 0.3% QoQ; all new disbursements placed under the CGFMU guarantee programme. Uncovered gross NPA of INR 296 crore sits under guarantee cover of INR 319 crore.

segments.name: NBFC term loans
segments.commentary: Growth of 0.7% YoY; management does not expect significant growth.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: CASA up 13% YoY; TD up 17.5% YoY; 96.1% of deposits have contractual tenor of 1 year and above.

guidance_outlook: PAT growth guidance raised to 100% YoY for FY27 from earlier 80%; management expects H2 PAT at least equal to H1 for this to hold.
Advances growth guidance maintained at 19-21%; deposit growth guidance maintained at 23-25%.
Full-year credit cost expected below 2%; H2 credit cost expected lower than H1's 0.92%.
Secured share of book expected to reach about 75% by year-end, versus 73.7% at Q2 and a long-term target of about 80%.
Cost-to-income targeted toward 60% over coming quarters; management says FY27 achievement is unlikely, with 57% (March 2024 level) as the first goal.
NIM expected to stay around current levels (about 7.5%) in H2 with cost of funds around 7.4%.
Guarantee claims of INR 68 crore expected to be received within about 2 months (by end-November); remaining INR 251 crore to be lodged in Q3 next year.

Branch expansion: 78 branches planned, 40 opened so far; launches planned for credit line on UPI (Q2 proof of concept), loans against shares and mutual funds (November), and trade FX via AD-1 licence (December).
capex_capacity: About 820 branches across India; 78 branch openings planned for FY27, with 40 completed by the call date.
Digital onboarding for non-face-to-face CASA accounts expected by January.
AI-led processes introduced in collections, welcome calling and cross-sell, reducing headcount and cost.
Headcount in September 2026 lower than March 2026 despite asset and liability growth.
demand_pricing: Q2 disbursements of INR 4,414 crore, up 7% YoY and 5% QoQ.
Affordable housing average ticket size INR 11.9 lakh; top seven states make up 67% of concentration, top three 37%.
Insurance income for H1 about INR 45 crore; 80-90% linked to credit life and 10-20% to retail products. IRDAI consultation impact not yet fully assessed.
Management says deposit pricing is fairly competitive; interest rates were harder in Q2 than Q1 and the market shows no sign of weakening rate regime.
Customers in the petroleum supply chain and related MSMEs show marginal impact; some export-linked sourcing paused because of higher shipping costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will slippages trend up or down in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects lower slippages in Q3 and H2. Q2 had one-offs: a secured loan slippage adding about 0.2% and drought-related MFI slippage of about 0.3%. SMA has graduated down in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of H1 insurance income is credit life and what is the IRDAI consultation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: 80-90% is credit life, 10-20% retail products. Initial IRDAI assessment done; full assessment pending. Management will push penetration and AI-led cost efficiency to offset lower commissions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cost-to-income decline sustainable and can it fall below 60%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost-to-income expected to stay at or below the September level; management is cautious that sub-60% is unlikely this year. Drivers are productivity, RPA/AI processes and more direct sourcing over DSA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CASA outlook and cost of funds risk from rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: CASA fell 2% QoQ in ratio terms but grew 13% YoY; management targets about 20% CASA in H2 via affluent offers and digital onboarding by January. Cost of funds targeted to stay near 7.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guarantee scheme cover the full book and what if it does not?
qa_highlights.answer: Claims of INR 68 crore lodged; NGC expected to pay within about 2 months. CGFMU is not open for fresh guarantees yet, but 1% cover cost has been accrued. If the scheme fails, the accrual becomes a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gold loan and micro LAP flat, and when will growth pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold flat due to 6-month loans from Jan-Mar 2026 renewing in Q2 and gold price drop; growth expected to resume in Q3 at about 10% a quarter. Micro LAP may reach 7-8% growth but not much more.

qa_highlights.question: Any risks to achieving 100% PAT growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no visible constraint on H2 profit matching H1; credit costs, asset growth and liability growth were all cited as on track.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM move in H2 amid rising rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NIM around current levels, as MFI share is not rising faster and secured share only reaches about 75%; cost of funds should not fall.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook by segment and do drought and geopolitical risks affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME 25-30% growth, affordable housing and vehicles continue strongly. Drought declared in 29 Karnataka districts and 34 Maharashtra districts; slippage impact expected to be immaterial. No material impact from the Iran war so far.

risks_watch: CGFMU guarantee scheme not yet open for fresh guarantees; if it does not reopen, the INR 296 crore uncovered unsecured NPA and future MFI risk rest on the bank's own buffer.
Net NPA at 1.08% is above the 1% comfort level until the INR 68 crore claim is received, expected by end-November.
CASA ratio fell and CASA growth (13% YoY) trails TD growth; deposit growth of 17% YoY is below the 23-25% guidance.
Drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra may lift slippages and moratorium requests; geopolitical oil and shipping cost impact on MSME exporters.

IRDAI insurance commission consultation could cut non-interest income; full impact not yet assessed. Media speculation about a merger, which management said it would evaluate if strategically sensible.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.why: CASA grew 13% YoY and fell 2% QoQ in ratio terms; management targets about 20% CASA via affluent offers and digital onboarding by January, but rate environment is tough and deposit pricing is competitive.

rows.label: AI-led headcount and cost reduction
rows.why: Headcount in September 2026 was lower than March 2026 despite asset and liability growth, and cost-to-income fell from 67.0% to 64.3% QoQ, with opex up 15% YoY against NII up 35%.

544119|2026-03.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, with PAT up 65% to INR 87 crores.
544119|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, EBITDA rose 41% with margin at 2.95%, and PAT grew 65% to INR 87 crores (1.93% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 15% to INR 15,827 crores, EBITDA rose 53% to INR 459 crores (2.90% margin, up 72 bps), and PAT rose 35% to INR 282 crores. Management attributed H2 growth mainly to price increases in the PES category, with H1 growth driven by volume and customer additions. Management guided to a ~20% CAGR and said the PC super cycle could last another 1-2 years, while flagging a possible 5-10% unit decline in CY26 and H2 consumer softness.

financial_highlights.change: Described as healthy vs prior-year outflows

segments.name: PES (Personal computing / enterprise)
segments.commentary: About 58% of business; grew 37% YoY in FY26, aided by higher H2 PC demand and ASPs. Management expects ~20% average price increase in this category going forward.

segments.name: LIT (Lifestyle IT)
segments.commentary: About 42% of business; grew 24% YoY in FY26. Price increases described as routine only; management says LIT is growing about 2x the industry.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Grew 131% YoY from a small base; customers include large automotive, robotics and IoT manufacturers. Operations moved into a newly created subsidiary; management says meaningful P&L impact is a few years away.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a ~20% CAGR (sustained for 20 years) and expects to maintain this trajectory in FY27; regular-business growth aspiration of 15-20% YoY.
Management estimates PES unit market could degrow 5-10% in CY26 (IDC concurs), but with 20-25% price growth, PES revenue could still grow 10-15% on an as-is basis.
Consumer demand could soften in H2 FY27 on affordability; management is discussing 24- and 36-month interest-free EMI schemes with vendors.
Working capital days expected to stay in a similar range in FY27 (CFO).
Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% considered applicable to the industry absent mix change; margins described as intact despite price hikes.
Management said the super cycle could continue for another 1-2 years.
Project business (AI data centre) planned for FY27 subject to viability and ROI; funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores under consideration.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 55 city branch offices with three new branches added (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur, Maharashtra); 10,000-plus customers across 700-plus towns.
Working capital was increased on inventory to capture demand; management said inventory days cannot fall while regular business grows ~30%.
Project business: FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores of AI data centre project (Yotta, 512 servers, 4,000 GPUs); no substantial project business in FY26; FY27 plans subject to ROI.
Semiconductor business moved into a separate subsidiary to focus operations and accelerate partnerships and customer acquisition.
Management says it has post-IPO capacity to pick up data centre projects on a selective ROI basis without compromising regular growth.
demand_pricing: Price increases began mainly in H2 FY26; management estimates roughly half of H2 growth (46-47% H2-on-H2) came from pricing, i.e. ~20-22 percentage points.
Management says FY26 growth ex the one large AI project was 31%; FY26 growth without large deals was 15% reported.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 growth reported at 42% and 51% respectively (non-project business).

AI PCs are about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India; NVIDIA DGX Spark and Dell (server, storage, PCs, monitors) partnerships cited; Dell described as at low-single-digit share of revenue, expected to reach close to double digits next FY.
IDC: India traditional PC shipments 15.9 million units in CY2025 (+10.2%); IDC flags possible 5-10% dip in CY2026 shipments.
Enterprise refresh delayed by some large corporates during price hikes is reversing as buyers see 30-40% higher prices a year later.
Management said demand is not softening currently; affordability risk in consumer segment in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of top-line growth came from pricing vs volume, and what is normalised growth for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were minimal in H1 and substantial in H2; H2 growth of 46-47% H2-on-H2 included about 20-22 points from price. Management reiterated 20% CAGR for 20 years and expects to maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is a PC classified as an AI PC, and how big is that segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices with an NPU or high-end processors/GPUs capable of AI workloads; about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India are AI PCs, expected to grow further over 1-2 years, lifting ASPs.

qa_highlights.question: Is refresh demand being delayed by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Some corporates extended refresh cycles initially, but the trend is reversing as buyers realise delay could cost 30-40% more; refresh expected to normalise as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Does the semiconductor business carry high working capital, and when will it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is higher (100-plus days cited), but gross margins and ROCE are higher than the regular business; the business is small, so meaningful margin impact is a few years away.

qa_highlights.question: How will RP Tech participate in AI data centre projects given capital needs and lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Funnels of about INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration; the company will pick projects selectively on ROI without compromising 15-20% regular growth; margins vary by project.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of revenue from large deals, enterprise and core distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 had no large AI deals (only INR 5-15 crore deals); enterprise non-AI growth is high, driven by NVIDIA solutions; growth ex-Yotta was 31%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ST Finserv channel finance programme affect working capital and credit risk?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a non-recourse channel finance programme for channel partners; the company bears no credit risk or funding cost unless it draws funds early, which it normally does not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT margin aspiration, and what caused the Q4 gross margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% is typical absent mix change; Q4 gross margin dip was due to additional provisioning for slow-moving inventory, not a structural decline.

risks_watch: Possible 5-10% unit decline in PC market in CY26 and H2 FY27 consumer softness from affordability as prices rise further.
Potential supply shortages in PES due to component (DRAM, NAND, GPU) pricing firmness.
Data centre project participation is capital-intensive with lower margins; scale of funnel conversion uncertain.
Inventory days (56) unlikely to fall while regular business grows ~30%; slow-moving inventory provision taken in Q4.
Semiconductor working capital cycle of 100-plus days; benefits to margin a few years away.
Dependence on Dell ramp-up (low-single-digit share now, expected near double-digit next FY).
544119|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the PC super cycle and multi-year growth, with growth targets reiterated. Evasive on specifics: declined to give Dell revenue numbers and deferred distribution-channel and margin-trajectory questions offline, and clarified several analyst misreadings of its figures.
key_quotes: So we are very confident to maintain our trajectory of 20% CAGR in the coming year as well.
This is not a 1-quarter tailwind. It is a structural multiyear upgrade super cycle.

Rashi will pick up proportionate to our capacity amongst these opportunities and obviously not run after everything because they are, one, capital intensive, and second, the margins are also lower on this front.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says distribution PAT margin of 1.5-1.75% is the industry-applicable range absent mix change; FY26 EBITDA margin 2.90% (+72 bps) was driven by price hikes, and Q4 gross margin was dented by slow-moving inventory provisioning, so further expansion is not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three new branches (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur) already commissioned, taking the network to 55 city branches; no plant or fixed-capacity capex is described, and the AI data centre project is subject to ROI with FY27 timing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: IDC flags a possible 5-10% dip in CY26 PC shipments and management flags H2 FY27 consumer affordability softness, so unit volumes are expected to fall even though revenue grows about 10-15% on 20-25% price increases.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only held at a ~20% revenue CAGR and 15-20% regular-business growth, with no raise, and FY26 growth was 15% reported (31% ex the large AI project).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consumer affordability risk and a possible 5-10% PES unit decline in CY26 could weigh on the 20% CAGR, and DRAM/NAND/GPU component pricing could cause supply shortages.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Dell ramp (low-single-digit share now, near double digits next FY) and AI PC mix (about 25% of Indian PCs/notebooks) are rising, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: AI data centre project funnel
rows.why: Funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration, but projects are subject to ROI and FY26 had no substantial project business (FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores Yotta project).

rows.label: PES price increases of ~20-25%
rows.why: Management expects ~20% average price increase in PES going forward; H2 FY26 pricing added about 20-22 points to H2 growth of 46-47%, and this supports PES revenue growth of 10-15% even as units fall 5-10%.

rows.label: Working capital days held
rows.why: CFO expects working capital days in a similar range (inventory 56, debtors 46, creditors 44, net 58 days), since inventory cannot fall while regular business grows about 30%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the PC super cycle, the 20% CAGR and the 1.5-1.75% PAT margin range, but evasive on Dell revenue numbers and deferred channel and margin questions offline; analysts probed price vs volume split, the Q4 gross margin dip and the AI data centre funnel.

544119|2026-06.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 62% YoY to Rs 5,102 crore, with PAT up 69% to Rs 105 crore and ROCE near 19.5%.
544119|2026-06.overview: Management reported record consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE for the quarter ended June 2026, driven by price increases in memory, storage and CPUs plus a rise in unit volume. Management said about 30-35% of the revenue growth came from price, 20-25% from quantity, 5-10% from new products and brands, and about 10% from market share gains. Pillars cited were the core distribution engine, the VDA Infosolutions acquisition (67% stake) and a semiconductor JV with Restar Japan (74:26). Management guided to similar growth in Q2 but a slower pace of price increases.

financial_highlights.change: up 55% YoY (CEO cited 50% on the opening remarks)

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 5,102 crore and PAT Rs 105 crore; management stated all-time highs on topline, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE.

segments.name: Commercial vs consumer (B2B mix)
segments.commentary: Management estimates 30-35% consumer-centric and 60-65% commercial (SMB and enterprise). Consumer demand is slowing on affordability, with laptop prices reportedly about 2x year-on-year.

segments.name: Semiconductor / embedded
segments.commentary: Semiconductor revenue in Q1 grew about 70% versus the Q1 FY26 base (not 70% of full-year revenue, per clarification). Growth is described as near double-digit and sometimes higher.

segments.name: VDA Infosolutions (acquired)
segments.commentary: Majority stake (67% in year one) in a pan-India system integrator; FY26 revenue was about Rs 850 crore. Management expects integrated services and value-added solutions to be about 5% of revenue, with Q2 as the next update point.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 growth expected to be similar to Q1 (about 60%), with price increase speed roughly halving; management described Q2 as on a strong footing.
Management expects the price uptrend to continue through FY27, with some slowdown in trajectory.
Management cited third-party reports of about a 10% unit decline in the overall PC market, offset by price increases.
Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record over 20 years; cited about Rs 3,000 crore as 20% of a Rs 16,000 crore base.
Semiconductor JV targets more than US$100 million revenue within three years; the JV numbers will be reported with Q2 results.
Large AI data centre deals not pursued aggressively in Q1 due to working-capital needs; management said the pipeline should last at least three quarters.
capex_capacity: Two new branches planned in Udaipur and Dhule to extend reach into C and D class cities.
Presence across 57 towns in India, per management.
Semiconductor JV Rashi Restar Semiconductor Solutions Private Limited to be formed as a step-down subsidiary; Restar to take 26% stake, with the existing embedded business moving into the JV.
Plans to add 50+ local engineering hires over the next two years for the semiconductor JV.
Debt-to-equity ratio cited at around 0.5; management said large data centre projects could push it to at least 2x.
demand_pricing: Memory, hard drive and CPU shortages are pushing prices higher; management expects the uptrend to continue through FY27.
Management said about 10% market share gain contributed to growth; unit growth ex-SanDisk was about 20%, with SanDisk unit declines pulling reported units lower.
Entry-level laptops face about 50% shortage per management; medium and premium notebooks available if prices are accepted.
T2 partners are holding elevated channel inventory to earn double-digit margins; management said it is not a concern given demand.
Refurbished PCs are seen as small: management estimated the refurbished pool at 0.5-1 million units against a 15-16 million PC TAM in India.
Management said Dell commercial business contributed about 5% of revenue in the quarter, and is above target for FY27.
Management said the company has allocations from NVIDIA, Intel and AMD; supply risk is tracked weekly ('orange alert').

qa_highlights.question: Why is India demand strong relative to global peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited economic strength, digitisation and education focus, plus data centre-related demand; commercial demand is holding up while consumer demand is slowing on affordability.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth between price, volume and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Price 30-35%, quantity 20-25%, new products and brands 5-10%, market share about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth match Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 should show a similar trend (about 60%), but the speed of price increases should roughly halve.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline: price or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix (higher PES share, lower margin than LIT) and to last year's hived-off subsidiary whose service cost sat in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply constraint risk in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is potential risk, but allocations so far are good given supplier relationships; the company tracks it weekly.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue large AI data centre deals aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised run-rate business with higher ROCE and working-capital needs; it still participates through smaller Rs 20-70 crore supplies and focuses on neo-clouds and smaller operators.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY28 look after the tailwinds fade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record and cited VDA and the Restar JV as longer-term growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor JV economics and Restar's investment amount?
qa_highlights.answer: Restar's investment depends on fair valuation at SPA signing, so it is not quantified; management targets over US$100 million JV revenue in three years and said the JV margin profile is higher than co-distribution.

Consumer affordability: consumer demand slowing with laptop prices about 2x YoY; management flagged possible consumer pressure in H2.
Channel inventory: T2 partners holding elevated inventory to earn double-digit margins; management said it is not a concern, but it is a watch item for price-driven sell-through.
Price increase pace: Q2 price increases expected to roughly halve; management said unit market may fall about 10% and growth depends on price offsetting volume.
Working capital and leverage: large AI data centre deals not pursued aggressively; management said debt-to-equity (around 0.5) could reach at least 2x if such projects are taken on.
Semiconductor JV: Restar's investment amount unquantified (depends on SPA valuation); JV numbers to be reported with Q2; VDA integration and contribution still undefined until Q2.

The only correction will happen on the speed of the price increase. Price increase speed should be half.
But yes, this is an orange alert for us. We track it on a weekly basis.
So, we are very optimistic that similar trend will continue in July-August-September also.
So, it is not that we are not there. It is only that we have not prioritized to do INR 500 crores or INR 1000 crores of deals

rows.why: Deals were not pursued aggressively in Q1 due to working-capital needs (working capital at 56 days); management says the pipeline should last at least three quarters, and D/E could reach 2x if taken on.
