544119|2026-09.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 42% YoY to INR5,708 crores and PAT 172% to INR153 crores, with ~30% of H1 growth from price increases.
544119|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 and H1 FY27 profits on both standalone and consolidated bases, with consolidated Q2 revenue up 49% YoY to INR6,185 crores and PAT up 121% to INR131 crores. Growth was driven mainly by price increases and volume, with VDA Infosolutions (67% stake) consolidated for only about one month and the Restar JV semiconductor business also contributing one month. Operating cash flow was negative for the half and net debt to equity rose to 0.76x, which management attributed to inventory built ahead of the delayed Diwali season and VDA funding. A possible QIP of about INR900 crores was flagged as advance preparation for growth capital, drawing investor pushback on dilution of about 15%.

segments.name: Core ICT distribution
segments.commentary: About 10-11% of H1 growth from volume, ~30% from price increases, and ~10% from new businesses. Non-PC products (accessories, peripherals, CPUs, motherboards, hard drives) are more than 35-37% of business, which management says carries extra margin.

segments.name: VDA Infosolutions (enterprise IT, 67% stake)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from Q2 for about one month; under 2% of Q2 revenue and about 6 bps of EBITDA contribution. Management targets new businesses (VDA plus semiconductor) above 10% of top line, with bottom line more than 2x.

segments.name: Semiconductor and embedded (Restar JV)
segments.commentary: JV formalised, consolidated for one month in Q2. Rashi did about $20 million of semiconductor business last year; H1 FY27 is about 2x that, with FY27 guided to 3-4x last year. Management says segment margins are about 2x company level.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 price increases expected to contribute 10-15% growth (down from ~30% in H1), with DRAM prices expected to rise for at least another year and flash/HDD prices flattening.
H2 unit volume guided as roughly flattish: consumer units expected to decline, commercial flat to positive.
Management is confident of maintaining a good run rate in H2, citing VDA, Restar JV and new product lines and territories.
Sustainable EBITDA margin for FY29-FY30 taken as around 2.75% as a safe planning assumption.
Interest cost expected to stay in the same range as H1, including acquisition debt interest.
Enterprise business targeted at about 20% of business in FY27 and FY28; the company has largely stayed out of large AI data centre projects so far.
Debt-to-equity to be kept at up to 1:1 barring temporary ROCE-led exceptions; a fresh raise of ~INR900 crores (QIP) is under preparation and may not happen.
capex_capacity: QIP preparation of about INR900 crores flagged as growth capital for capacity; management said at 1:1 debt-equity it would add INR1,800-2,000 crores of deployable capital and support INR12,000-15,000 crores of additional revenue on a 6-7x working capital cycle.
Inventory built in Sept-Oct to secure supply and committed enterprise and AI projects; management plans to convert it to cash in H2 and report progress next quarter.
Depreciation run rate after VDA consolidation is about INR12 crores per quarter, including intangibles amortisation; ESOP cost in Q2 was INR3.8 crores.
Restar JV plans a design centre in Bangalore with one Restar engineer deputed to train the team; Restar has around 200 engineers in Tokyo.
demand_pricing: IDC reported India PC market grew about 12% in April-June quarter, led by commercial, education and small business demand, with premium and AI-capable notebooks.
Management flagged that part of channel buying was ahead of price increases and that higher prices are hitting consumer affordability; commercial is about 70% of India's ICT market.
Deepavali shifted from 20 October (2025) to 8 November (2026), delaying the cycle about one month; October sales were described as very good and the current week continues strong.
Semiconductor distribution opportunity in India estimated at about INR25,000 crores; Restar's market reach estimated at about 10% of opportunity, leaving about 90% unserved.
Post-COVID price correction of 10-15% did not hurt distribution; Rashi grew about 7% while the market declined about 15%, per the CEO.
Enterprise and AI data centre orders of more than INR20,000 crores were placed in the last quarter; Rashi chose not to bid aggressively.
Management said it had 89 global brands, 10,280 channel partners, 57 branches, 50 service centres and 728 locations.

qa_highlights.question: Why was inventory built so strongly this quarter given softening consumer demand, and why a QIP of about INR900 crores (~15% dilution)?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was built for the Diwali timing shift (one-month delay) and October sales were strong; management called the consumer impact minuscule. The QIP is advance preparation for growth capital and may not be done if not needed; an analyst suggested a calibrated raise instead.

qa_highlights.question: Split of growth between volume, price and VDA?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth of about 50% was split roughly 30% price, 10-11% volume and about 10% new businesses. VDA contributed under 2% of Q2 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How is margin resilient in a seasonally strong quarter, and how much is value-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong demand, price increases reducing market price competition, and a non-PC mix (35-37%) with margin opportunities. It said the margin is sustainable near term.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Restar JV bring and is it exclusive?
qa_highlights.answer: It brings Japanese brands (two large ones already added, distribution starting this month), design capability, and access to Japanese manufacturers in India (meetings with 5 this month). Arrangements may be a mix of exclusive and non-exclusive; names not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Price outlook for H2 and risk of price correction?
qa_highlights.answer: Price contribution to growth is expected at 10-15% in H2 versus ~30% in H1. DRAM prices are expected to rise for at least another year, while flash and HDD have flattened.

qa_highlights.question: Debt-to-equity and funding plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is up to 1:1 debt-equity; the current 0.76x net debt-to-equity includes acquisition debt. Growth to be funded by internal accruals, debtor factoring and, if required, a capital raise. September quarter is the peak for borrowings.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow for H1 and net debt to equity of 0.76x; management promised inventory conversion progress next quarter.
Consumer demand expected to decline in units in H2; price increases are expected to slow to 10-15% contribution.
Possible QIP of about INR900 crores (~15% dilution) and investor reaction to its size and timing.
Integration of VDA (67% stake) and the newly formed Restar semiconductor JV; execution and retention of staff and clients.
Large enterprise and AI data centre projects were not pursued aggressively, so H2 contribution from this area is uncertain.
Sharp increase in intangibles from the VDA acquisition, with goodwill below 20% of the total intangibles.
544119|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, but explicitly cautious on consumer demand and credit; management acknowledged cash flow and leverage pressure and framed it as deliberate. Several answers on the QIP size, JV exclusivity and AI exposure were general or deferred until formalisation.
key_quotes: So, the expansion is coming from mix and pricing discipline, not only operating leverage.
Converting the cash inventory into cash in the second half is a priority, and we will report on our progress next quarter.
So, the impact so far is miniscule.
Broadly, it is 2x on margin front.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 standalone EBITDA margin rose 95 bps YoY to 3.44% and H1 to 3.28%, but management plans around 2.75% sustainable for FY29-FY30, implying H2 margins are not guaranteed to hold at the Q2 level.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: A ~INR900 crore QIP is under preparation for growth capital, which at 1:1 debt-equity would add INR1,800-2,000 crore of deployable capital supporting INR12,000-15,000 crore of revenue, but the raise may not happen; the Bangalore Restar design centre is engineering, not production, capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H2 unit volume is guided roughly flattish, with consumer units expected to decline and only commercial flat to positive, versus about 10-11% volume growth in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is preparing a ~INR900 crore QIP for growth capital, but utilisation was not disclosed and the company is asset-light distribution, so the call hinges on the QIP going ahead.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H2 price contribution is guided down to 10-15% from ~30% in H1 and units flattish, so growth guidance is more likely to moderate than rise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative, net debt to equity rose to 0.76x, consumer units are expected to fall in H2, and price-led growth roughly halves to 10-15%, though management is confident of maintaining a good H2 run rate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cites new product lines and territories, including two large Japanese brands added via the Restar JV with distribution starting this month, and semiconductor FY27 targeted at 3-4x last year's roughly $20 million base.

rows.label: Inventory conversion to cash in H2
rows.why: Working capital days fell to 55 from 61 a year ago, and management plans to convert the Sept-Oct inventory build to cash in H2 and report progress next quarter, but H1 operating cash flow was negative.

rows.label: Semiconductor and VDA above 10% of top line
rows.why: Management targets new businesses above 10% of revenue with bottom line more than 2x, and semiconductor H1 is about 2x last year's ~$20 million, guided to 3-4x for FY27.

rows.label: Enterprise and AI data centre participation
rows.why: Enterprise and AI orders above INR20,000 crore were placed last quarter but Rashi chose not to bid aggressively, though it still targets enterprise at about 20% of business.

tone.note: Management was confident on record profits, margins and the Restar/VDA growth push, but cautious on consumer demand, cash flow and leverage; analysts pressed on the ~INR900 crore QIP dilution (~15%), inventory build, and JV exclusivity and AI exposure, which were answered only generally.

544120|2026-03.headline: Capital SFB Q4 FY26 PAT rose 17% YoY to ₹40 crores, with NIM up to 4.06% and FY27 ROA guided to 1.35%–1.4%.
544120|2026-03.overview: Gross advances reached ₹8,687 crores (+20.9% YoY, +6.4% QoQ) and total deposits crossed ₹10,000 crores (+20% YoY). Q4 PPOP rose 28% YoY to ₹62 crores and cost of deposits eased to 5.75% from 5.86% QoQ, with NIM at 4.06% versus 4.01% in Q3. Asset quality was broadly stable: GNPA 2.54%, NNPA 1.24%, with Q4 credit cost of 0.26% driven by higher provisioning (PCR 51.89%) rather than losses. Management guided to FY27 advances growth of 22%+, ROA of 1.35%–1.4%, and credit cost of 0.15%–0.25%.

segments.name: MSME / business banking
segments.commentary: Growth driver: +9% QoQ and +46% YoY in Q4. Management expects it to remain a growth leader in FY27.

segments.name: LAP (loan against property)
segments.commentary: +5% QoQ and +19% YoY; yield 12.33% in Q4 vs 12.56% in Q3. Named as a FY27 growth leader.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Book grew 7% QoQ but net NPA was static at 2.76% vs 2.75%. Growth to be slower than the overall book, limited to Punjab and Haryana.

segments.name: Mortgage / housing
segments.commentary: Housing yield 9.85% in Q4 vs 9.83% in Q3. Cited as a driver for growth in newer states.

segments.name: NBFC-MFI
segments.commentary: Outstanding net NPA ₹5.49 crores vs ₹6.08 crores a quarter earlier; total exposure about ₹39 crores. No fresh lending in Q4; an OTS was signed with one lender.

segments.name: Out-of-Punjab advances
segments.commentary: 24% of advances at March 2026 vs 21% a year earlier; growing more than twice the Punjab rate YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 secured advances growth of 22%+; advances above ₹16,000 crores by FY29.
Branches: target of 235 by end of FY27 (current year) and 300+ by FY29.
NIM expected to improve slightly in Q1 FY27 and more meaningfully in Q2; 53% of term deposits are high-priced and reprice in the next two quarters.
FY27 ROA target of 1.35%–1.4%, rising to 1.6%+ by FY29; ROE of 15%+ by FY29.
FY27 opex/average assets guided to 2.9%–3.0% (lower bias), with opex/average assets below 2.85% over the medium term.
FY27 credit cost guided to 0.15%–0.25% with negative bias; target of about 0.3% up to FY29.
Fee income/average assets guided to 0.85%–0.95% with upward bias; Banca to be expanded by one product in FY27 and one more later.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 211 across 5 states and 2 union territories at March 2026; 77.3% are SURU branches.
Target of 235 branches by end of FY27 and 300+ by FY29; 50% of new branches to be opened outside Punjab and 40–45% in Punjab.
Management said cost of new branches in FY27 is mainly last-mile branch cost, as senior and head-office costs are already built in.
Business per branch (5+ year branches) is ₹106 crores in Punjab vs ₹73 crores outside Punjab; PPOP of 5+ year branches is 2.75%–3.25% vs 2.1% entity level.
demand_pricing: Disbursements were ₹919 crores in Q4 (+20% YoY) and ₹3,508 crores in FY26 (+23% YoY).
Average ticket size ₹18.3 lakh vs ₹17.8 lakh in Q3; about 98% of the book is secured and about 89% of the non-corporate book is backed by property or FDRs.

Yields: agriculture 12.54% (vs 12.62%), business 10.55% (vs 10.6%), corporate 10.77% (vs 10.8%); overall advance yield fell to about 10.8% from about 11.1%, partly due to a 25 bps rate cut and agri accounts moving to NPA with interest reversals.
Fee income was ₹25.8 crores in Q4 vs ₹26.1 crores in Q3 (0.9% of assets, vs 1.0% a year earlier); treasury income fell due to weaker market opportunities.
Cost of deposits 5.75% in Q4 vs 5.86% in Q3; average CD ratio 82.3%, period-end 86.7%; retail deposits above 90%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross NPA additions and provisioning: are provisions increasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹22 crore FY provision figure includes tax; PCR was raised to 51.89% from 50.45%, so provisioning was increased within the profit outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Agri NPA stickiness: will it fall back toward 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not target 2%; it expects agri NPA to stay range-bound with a lower bias. Recoveries concentrate in Q1 and Q3 cash-flow periods.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new ECL framework on credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial view is P&L neutral to positive, as current provisions are considered sufficient against the ECL requirement; detailed evaluation is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Co-lending / BC model and FLDG cover?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank runs a business correspondent lending model (not co-lending) with more than one partner, and the FLDG cover is 5% per regulation. Branches are to remain 90–95% of disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the NII margin expansion and CD ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Term deposit repricing (53% repricing in Q1–Q2) and an improving CD ratio are the two NIM levers; management expects an opex/average assets ratio of 2.9%–3.0% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost for FY27 is 0.15%–0.25%. The Q4 credit cost of 0.26% was provisioning-driven, linked to NBFC-MFI slippage. Cost-to-income is expected to improve, with opex/average assets at 2.9%–3.0%.

risks_watch: Agri asset quality: net NPA at 2.76%, and monsoon or input-cost stress could affect the book, although management cites Punjab irrigation and collateral.
Pace of deposit repricing and whether NIM reaches the guided improvement in Q1–Q2 FY27.
Yield pressure: advance yields fell to about 10.8% amid rate cuts and NPA reversals; 8–10 bps of the decline is described as temporary.
Fee income and treasury income momentum; Banca and fee targets depend on new product approvals.
ECL transition impact, which management expects to be P&L neutral to positive but is still under evaluation.
Growth outside Punjab through business correspondent partners, which is early-stage and carries FLDG exposure.
544120|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and detailed on growth and margin guidance, with specific numeric targets for FY27 and FY29. Management was defensive on agriculture NPA stickiness and the 0.26% credit cost, attributing both to provisioning and seasonality rather than losses.
key_quotes: So we are seeing some benefit, which will be pouring up from that repricing on their maturity.
So the current quarter credit cost is a provisioning driven, not a loss driven.
We are not doing agriculture in Rajasthan, UP, in Jammu, Himachal.

Q4 vs 1.16% in Q3 and 1.36% in Q4 FY25

rows.why: Q4 PAT rose 17% YoY and ROA reached 1.33% in Q4 vs 1.16% in Q3, but FY27 ROA guide of 1.35%–1.4% is only modestly above the 1.23% FY26 level, so an upgrade depends on sustaining the Q4 run rate.

rows.why: Agri net NPA is 2.76% and stuck, NBFC-MFI slippage drove the 0.26% Q4 credit cost against a FY27 guide of 0.15%–0.25%, and yields fell to ~10.8% from ~11.1%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans to expand Banca by one product in FY27 and one more later, and fee income guidance of 0.85%–0.95% of average assets depends on new product approvals.

rows.label: Term deposit repricing lifts NIM
rows.why: 53% of term deposits are high-priced and reprice in the next two quarters, with cost of deposits already down to 5.75% from 5.86% QoQ.

rows.label: Opex/average assets held at 2.9%-3.0%
rows.why: Cost-to-income fell to 58.2% in Q4 from 61% for FY26, and the 5+ year branches run PPOP of 2.75%-3.25% vs 2.1% at entity level, with new branches mainly last-mile cost.

rows.label: Out-of-Punjab growth via BC partners
rows.why: Out-of-Punjab advances are 24% of the book vs 21% a year earlier, and 50% of new branches are to open outside Punjab, though the BC model is early-stage with 5% FLDG exposure.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 22%+ FY27 growth, NIM repricing, and branch build-out to 235, and defensive on agri NPA stickiness and the 0.26% Q4 credit cost, which it attributed to provisioning. Analysts pressed on asset quality and provisioning.

544120|2026-06.headline: Capital SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 41.3 crore, with NIM at 4.21% and GNPA down to 2.47%.
544120|2026-06.overview: Gross advances reached INR 9,074 crore, up 22% YoY and 4.5% QoQ, while deposits grew 16% YoY to INR 10,596 crore with CASA at 36.7%. NIM improved to 4.21% from 4.06% a year ago, helped by deposit repricing and a higher average CD ratio of 83%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.47% and NNPA at 1.14%, as the bank raised PCR to 54.5%. Management guided to stable NIM near 4.2% for FY27, ROA of 1.35-1.4% for FY27, and 22% advance growth.

financial_highlights.change: from 4.06% in Q4 FY26 and 4.06% in Q1 FY26
GNPA -28 bps YoY, -7 bps QoQ; NNPA from 1.39% YoY and 1.24% QoQ
broadly in line with last year

segments.name: Business loans (MSME and other)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 27% of book (22% a year ago) and 35% of incremental disbursements; MSME grew 49% YoY and 11% QoQ, with average ticket INR 28 lakh and yield on business loans at 10.5%.

segments.name: Mortgage
segments.commentary: Stable at 25% of book (around 26% a year ago); grew 3% QoQ and 10% YoY, with housing yield at 9.87% vs 9.85% in Q4 FY26; average housing ticket INR 20-25 lakh.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Share fell to about 27% from 30% a year ago; target ticket INR 5-35 lakh (average INR 30 lakh), with yields of 12-12.5% over the last 7-9 quarters and 50% LTV collateral.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Stable at 14% of book; calibrated lending to well-rated corporates.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: Yield of 12.27%; grew 5% QoQ and 18% YoY.

segments.name: Consumption loans
segments.commentary: Stable at around 7% of book, mostly top-up loans; 2-3% of the book is loan against deposits or securities.

segments.name: Geography

qa_highlights.question: Split of MSME growth between Punjab and Haryana, and how it is trending
qa_highlights.answer: MSME (INR 28 lakh average ticket, middle-income, collateralised) grew 49% YoY and 11% QoQ; growth within Punjab and outside Punjab, and between Punjab and Haryana, is similar. Advances outside Punjab are 25% of the book vs 24% a quarter ago and 21% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why PCR has been rising over recent quarters and whether it will stay stable
qa_highlights.answer: PCR was raised to 54.5% to move net NPA towards the medium-term 1% target; management says most of that action is done and it expects a stable PCR from here.

qa_highlights.question: Headroom for cost of deposit repricing and ROA path
qa_highlights.answer: Remaining repricing is not material; the bulk was done in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27. ROA is targeted at 1.35-1.4% in FY27 and 1.6%+ by FY29; Q1 ROA was 1.3% vs 1.18%, and PPOP margin rose to 2.04% from 1.94%.

qa_highlights.question: What keeps NIM stable at around 4.2% given cost-of-deposit and yield pressure
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,597 crore of term deposits reprice in Q2 FY27 for a 10-12 bps benefit, which management expects to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs. Advance yield fell to 10.9% from 11.1%; 50% of the book is fixed and 50% floating; NIM expansion is expected in FY28-29 as average CD ratio (83%) rises to mid-to-high 80s.

qa_highlights.question: Why PSU competition in housing eased and whether mortgage growth will pick up
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit repricing helped the bank compete with PSBs in the INR 20-25 lakh housing ticket; mortgage grew 3% QoQ and 10% YoY at a 9.87% yield vs 9.85% in Q4, but management says growth will stay moderate with some portion still to be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Agri yield levels and risk mitigation
qa_highlights.answer: Agri average ticket is INR 30 lakh (range INR 5-35 lakh), with yields of 12-12.5% over the last 7-9 quarters, priced 25-35 bps over PSB rates in the INR 5-25 lakh band; collateral LTV is 50%, and management attributes the premium to industry-wide risk perception.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 repricing of about INR 1,597 crore of term deposits: the 10-12 bps benefit is expected to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs, so NIM holding at about 4.2% depends on this.
Advance yield has fallen to 10.9% from 11.1%, and the business loan yield is 10.5%; further yield compression would pressure the 5.05-5.3% spread target.
SMA-2 rose to 3.11% from 2.71% in the quarter, though total SMA-1 and SMA-2 fell to 4.78% from 5.47% a year ago; management called the rise not meaningful.
Opex at 2.95-2.98% of assets; management expects a moderate FY27 increase, with larger opex growth in FY29, which could weigh on the ROA path.
Average CD ratio of 83% needs to reach mid-to-high 80s; management says advance growth will outpace deposit growth in Q2 and Q4, and deposit growth is strongest in Q1 and Q3.
Universal bank conversion depends on getting net NPA to about 1%, which the bank currently reports at 1.14%.

rows.why: Management reaffirmed 22% FY27 advance growth against gross advances of INR 9,074 crore (+22% YoY) and deposits +16% YoY, with MSME growing 49% YoY and fresh disbursements +17% YoY to INR 1,009 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Average CD ratio at 83% is well below the 80%+ utilisation threshold framing for a capex trigger, the bank has 216 branches and CAR is 21.6%, and capex was not discussed on the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 guidance (22% advance growth, ROA 1.35-1.4%) rather than raising it, with Q1 ROA at 1.3% and opex to rise moderately in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: SMA-2 rose to 3.11% from 2.71% in the quarter and advance yield fell to 10.9% from 11.1%, which could pressure the 5.05-5.3% spread target and the 1.35-1.4% ROA path if not offset.

rows.label: Net NPA glide path to about 1% (universal bank conversion)
rows.why: Net NPA is 1.14% after PCR was raised to 54.5%, and management expects stable PCR from here, so further NNPA reduction is guided but not yet dated within 2-4 quarters.

rows.label: Term deposit repricing benefit in Q2 FY27
rows.why: About INR 1,597 crore of term deposits reprice for a 10-12 bps benefit, but management expects this to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs, so net gain is uncertain.

rows.label: CD ratio rise from 83% toward mid-to-high 80s
rows.why: Average CD ratio is 83% (vs 80.9% a year ago); reaching mid-to-high 80s implies a 3-6% shift of investments and interbank balances (yielding 7-7.5%) into advances at 10.5-11%.

tone.note: Management was confident on 22% advance growth, ROA 1.35-1.4% and asset quality/PCR stability, but cautious on housing recovery and on how much cost-of-deposit repricing remains; analysts pushed on NIM sustainability given falling advance yield (10.9% from 11.1%).

544120|2026-09.headline: Capital SFB Q2 FY27: gross advances up 23.4% YoY to INR9,755 crore, PAT up about 31% to INR46 crore, NIM 4.24%.
544120|2026-09.overview: Gross advances grew 23.4% YoY and 7.5% QoQ to INR9,755 crore, with disbursements of INR1,095 crore (up 36% YoY). Total deposits reached INR10,831 crore (up 16.2% YoY), with CASA at 34.5% and cost of deposits down to 5.68% from 5.92% a year ago. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.36% and net NPA at 1.12%, while PPOP of INR68 crore and PAT of INR46 crore rose about 31% YoY. Management reiterated the Vision 2029 targets of over INR16,000 crore loan book and 300-plus branches, and flagged a possible regulatory change to bancassurance income.

segments.name: Business loans
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 28% of the book, up from 23% a year ago and 27% last quarter. Management said business loans are growing faster than the overall book.

segments.name: Mortgages (LAP)
segments.commentary: About 24% of advances, down from 26% a year ago and 25% last quarter.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: About 26% of advances, down from 27% last quarter. Agri grew 6.23% QoQ; lending is confined to Punjab and Haryana.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Held deliberately flat at about 14% of advances, lending only to well-rated borrowers.

segments.name: Consumption
segments.commentary: About 7% of portfolio, growing 6.89% QoQ and 21.9% YoY; net NPA 0.47%. Offered mainly as a second or third product to existing customers.

segments.name: Punjab vs outside Punjab
segments.commentary: Outside Punjab has 21% of branches (47), 25.7% of advances and 8.2% of deposits. Outside-Punjab advances grew 39% YoY vs 19% for Punjab; GNPA 0.87% outside vs 2.88% in Punjab.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan growth guidance was 20-22% at the start of the year; H1 growth was 23%, and management said it is aiming to overachieve.
Vision 2029 targets: gross advances over INR16,000 crore and more than 300 branches by FY29. Management said the current run rate exceeds what is needed.
ROA target of 1.6% by FY29 from 1.39% today, driven by NIM expansion (guided 4.3-4.35%, a 7-12 bps gain) and opex (operating cost to average assets guided 2.80-2.85% by FY29 from about 3.05%).
Target net NPA below 1%.
Target of 30%+ branches outside Punjab by FY29, with out-of-Punjab advances expected at 32-37% of the book.
Universal bank license aspiration after FY29, at a balance sheet of about INR21,000-23,000 crore.
capex_capacity: Network of 222 branches across 5 states and 2 union territories; 77% of branches are in semi-urban and rural centres (SURU), contributing 75% of deposits.
Business per branch outside Punjab reached INR80 crore-plus for branches of 5 years and above, vs INR72 crore at end-Q4 FY26.
Target of more than 300 branches by FY29, with 30%+ outside Punjab.
Rajasthan presence is limited to 7 branches; the bank is following an asset-first approach in new geographies such as Rajasthan and NCR.
Capital adequacy ratio of 20.8% (Tier 1 18.5%), with no immediate need to raise fresh capital.
demand_pricing: Industry credit grew about 19.4% YoY vs deposit growth of about 17.8% as of September 2026.
RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% in October 2026 and moved to calibrated tightening; management expects rates to stay higher for longer.
Yield on advances was 11% in Q2 FY27, flat YoY and up 10 bps QoQ. The October repo hike has not yet flowed into advance yields.
About 52% of advances are fixed-rate and 48% floating; EBR-linked loans are 13-14% of the portfolio and get a 25 bps EBR increase from 1 November 2026.
Term deposit ATS is about INR12 lakh; savings average ticket is about INR50,000. Retail deposits are over 90% of the total, with rollover above 90%.
Management sees its deposit premium at 25-35 bps over top private sector universal banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the weak monsoon affecting the agriculture book, and is collection efficiency holding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is not visible in Punjab and Haryana, citing canal water and tube wells. H1 gross slippage was 1.11% annualised, net slippage 0.24%, and SMA1+2 fell to 3.31%. Early paddy productivity data is the same or better than last year in 25 of 26 districts.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the cost of deposits fallen only 22 bps when the RBI cut rates by 125 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank has a premium over peers, a CASA ratio above 34%, and fixed-rate TD repricing. About 60-62% of the benefit has come through repricing, and the cost of deposits is 5.68%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM path and the scope to expand it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided NIM to 4.3-4.35% from 4.24%, citing a CD ratio move from 85.4% toward the mid-to-high 80s over 1.5-2 years. It said this can happen without changing deposit or loan pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are consumption-loan yields low, and will the bank go to fresh customers via dealers?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption loans are about 7% of the book, mainly cross-sell to existing customers. About 25-30% is loan against own FDRs at 7.5-8%. Management said pilots are running to fast-track sub-products, but it did not give details.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the draft IRDAI circular on bancassurance, and what is the other fee income plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Bancassurance commission was INR10.2 crore out of INR30 crore non-interest income, about 33%. Management said the bank is waiting for a draft circular, expects an impact that is not material, and cited a 0.92% non-interest income-to-assets ratio. The ROA plan does not rely on fee income.

qa_highlights.question: What are the universal bank aspirations and when will they be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims to apply for a universal bank licence after FY29, at a balance sheet of about INR21,000-23,000 crore, once the bank reaches the FY29 targets.

risks_watch: Weak monsoon and drought in parts of India (management said Punjab and Haryana remain unaffected); watch agri slippages and SMA trends.
Margin pressure if deposit repricing outpaces the loan-yield pass-through in a higher-for-longer rate cycle; yield on advances was flat YoY at 11%.
Bancassurance fee income (about 33% of non-interest income) at risk from the IRDAI draft circular; the bank has not yet detailed alternatives.
Growth and profitability outside Punjab: CASA there is 25.3% vs 35.3% in Punjab, and outside-Punjab deposits are only 8.2% of the total.
CASA ratio fell QoQ (seasonal, per management) in a high term deposit rate environment.
544120|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and the Vision 2029 targets, with management saying it is growth-hungry and that the run rate exceeds plan. More measured on rates and the IRDAI draft, where it said it is waiting for a draft circular and declined to size the alternatives.
key_quotes: Our priorities are quite simple, remain the same, grow the franchise, strengthen the deposit base and protect the quality of the balance sheet.
We are a growth-hungry organization, and we believe the complete foundation is available to grow.
We will keep lending the way we always have, secured, granular with careful customer selection and strong collection.

544122|2026-03.headline: Entero FY26 revenue rose 31.5% like-for-like to INR6,591 crore with 4% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance is 23% growth and 5% margin excluding new acquisitions.
544122|2026-03.overview: FY26 met all three initial targets: like-for-like revenue growth of 31.5% (organic 15.6%, inorganic 16%), 4% EBITDA margin (+67 bps) and operating cash flow of INR96.2 crore. Q4 revenue grew 42.6% YoY, with organic growth of 17.1% and acquisitions contributing 26%, and Q4 EBITDA margin reached 4.5%. Minority interest jumped sharply in Q4 (about 38% of PAT) due to an abnormal, pulled-forward MedTech sale at a partly-owned subsidiary, which management says will normalise. FY27 guidance is 23% consolidated revenue growth excluding new acquisitions (about 11 points from calendarisation), 5% EBITDA margin, and at least 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Now above INR1,000 crore annualised revenue after 3 MedTech acquisitions in FY26 (Anand Chemiceutics, Ace Cardiopathy, Bio de Technology). Management says MedTech is over 15% of revenue, could reach about 20% in 2-3 years, and earns higher margins than pharma due to commercial/agency role.

segments.name: Pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Remains the core business with about 100,000 retail pharmacies, 3,600 hospitals, 97,500 SKUs and 3,300+ manufacturers. Management expects pharma and MedTech to contribute equally to FY27 organic growth.

segments.name: GLP-1
segments.commentary: Management says current GLP-1 sales are about INR10-12 crore per month, roughly 5% of industry GLP value, with a share above its overall India share due to cold-chain warehouses; included in FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 23% YoY excluding new acquisitions; about 11 points from calendarisation of FY26 acquisitions and the rest organic (management also cited about 22% in one answer).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 5%, about 50 bps above Q4 FY26's 4.5%, from MedTech mix, operating leverage and exiting low-margin businesses.
EBITDA-to-operating cash flow conversion of at least 50% in FY27.
Tax rate of about 22-23% for FY27.
Minority interest to be about 25-27% of PAT before minority interest in FY27, down from about 38% in Q4.
Finance cost to stay relatively stable for a couple of quarters, then decline over the next couple of years as IPO funds were used up.
No new acquisitions assumed for the next 6-8 months; guidance would be revised upwards if acquisitions are made. Acquisitions are priced at 5-7x EV/EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Seven acquisitions closed in FY26, including 3 in MedTech; management says no new acquisitions are planned for the next 6-8 months, focusing on organic growth.
Some MedTech IVD machines are placed at customer sites on 5-year reagent rental contracts and are depreciated; cardiology and other MedTech lines carry little depreciating equipment.
Cold-chain facilities in all warehouses support GLP-1 distribution.
Depreciation rose about 50% QoQ in Q4, and interest costs rose because acquisitions were debt- or investment-funded after IPO proceeds were used up.
demand_pricing: Organic growth outperformed IPM by 1.6x for FY26 (15.6% vs IPM); Q3 and Q4 multiplier fell to about 1.4x as IPM grew about 12% versus 7-8% earlier, while organic growth stayed at 16-17%.
FY27 like-for-like growth is about 15% (1.5x IPM) per management; some low-ROIC businesses are being exited and some are now booked on a net-revenue basis, lowering reported revenue.
Gross margin gains come from scale purchasing and a commercial/agency role; full commercial role accounts for 10-15%+ of sales, with margins at least double normal distribution margins.
Management pointed to the 8-15% gross margin band on slide 28 for distribution; Q4 gross margin was 10.9%.
Middle East conflict: direct imports are a very small share of sales, so management says the company is largely insulated.

qa_highlights.question: Why did minority interest jump in Q4 and how much will it be in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 minority interest was abnormally high, about 38% of PAT, due to a customer pulling forward equipment sales at a partly-owned subsidiary. FY27 minority share is guided at about 25-27% of pre-minority PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 23% FY27 growth include calendarisation and GLP-1?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Calendarisation is about 11 points, and GLP-1 is built into guidance, with the company taking a disproportionate share given its cold-chain network.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital falling, and how much working capital will FY27 growth need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop mainly to higher payables from MedTech, which has longer credit terms than pharma. Q4 annualised revenue of about INR7,600-8,000 crore means most working capital is already in the balance sheet, so incremental needs should be small.

qa_highlights.question: Will acquisitions continue, and at what valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: No new acquisitions are assumed for 6-8 months. Valuations remain 5-7x EV/EBITDA, and call options on remaining stakes are pre-agreed, typically over 3 to 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 ROCE above 20%, with further upside possible over time, though not necessarily in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's competitive moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a two-way network: about 100,000 customers and over 3,000 manufacturers. It said retail consolidation will stay limited, with chains under 15,000 stores versus over 1 million pharmacies.

risks_watch: Minority interest of 25-27% of PAT in FY27 materially reduces attributable earnings; watch for further put-option liability effects on net worth, which was flat in FY26.
Finance cost is expected to stay stable for a couple of quarters before declining; interest and depreciation rose sharply in Q4.
IPM growth outperformance has narrowed to about 1.4x as IPM rose to about 12%; FY27 organic growth depends on sustaining this.
FY28 growth not guided; management will provide more visibility in H2 FY27.
Payables-driven working capital improvement may reverse if MedTech mix or credit terms change; the 50% EBITDA-to-OCF target depends on this.
544122|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on delivering FY26 targets and on FY27 margin expansion, but guarded on FY28 and interest costs. Management deflected several questions on minority interest and acquisition pipeline and offered to share some data offline.
key_quotes: We aim for consolidated revenue growth of 23% year-on-year, excluding any new acquisitions with 5% EBITDA margins.
So in some of the cases, it's a 3-year period. In some cases, it could be 5 year.
So it's a 2-way moat. It's a 2-way closed-loop system.

544122|2026-06.headline: Entero Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore and EBITDA margin reached 5.0%, already meeting full-year FY27 margin guidance.
544122|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore (40% like-for-like), with organic growth of 17.8% reported and 19.6% like-for-like versus an underlying pharma market growth of 13.8%. Gross margin expanded 147 bps to 11.4% and EBITDA margin expanded 143 bps to 5.0%, with EBITDA up 94% YoY. PAT rose 72% YoY to INR52 crore, but PAT attributable to owners was INR38 crore (up 37%) after INR14 crore of non-controlling interest. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~23% revenue growth ex-acquisitions, 5% EBITDA margin and 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion, and said no major acquisitions are planned in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: entirely calendarisation of prior-year acquisitions; no new acquisitions in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR14 crore (~27% of PBT before minority interest)
financial_highlights.change: Q4 was about INR17 crore per the call

segments.name: Core pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Majority of business is demand fulfilment with lower gross margins; margin gains attributed to scale-driven procurement. Low-margin sub-distribution accounts exited, which reduced reported growth by about 2.5%.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Organic MedTech revenue on track to exceed INR1,000 crore in FY27 and carries higher gross and EBITDA margins than core pharma. Management said the business plays a demand-generation role, not only fulfilment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: consolidated revenue growth of ~23% YoY excluding new acquisitions (about 11-12 points from calendarisation of prior acquisitions, rest organic).
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 5% maintained; management aspires to improve further and said H2 could beat guidance depending on H1 performance.
EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion of 50% on an annual basis; OCF is after working capital changes.
FY27 effective tax rate guidance of 22.5%; FY28 guidance to be given near FY27 close.
Interest cost expected to stay broadly in the same range as Q1 for the rest of the year.
Employee cost increments fell mainly in Q1 (effective 1 April); no major increase expected thereafter.

Medium-term: management said it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and modelling 20% is a safe assumption; ROCE of 25-30% was cited as possible in that period; internal aspiration EBITDA margin above 6%.
No revision to working capital days guidance; management will review after H1.
capex_capacity: Platform: 138 warehouses across 475 districts in 19 states; 72,000+ retail customers, 2,300+ hospital customers, 83,400+ SKUs, 3,000+ manufacturer relationships.
Depreciation: Q1 level expected to be the going-forward run-rate, subject to any major new capex; Q4 included depreciation on certain machines given to customers.
No major acquisitions planned for FY27, though a pipeline exists; a small Andhra Pradesh surgical consumables deal (with Sai Pharma) was completed and is immaterial to revenue.
Around INR200 crore of debt was taken for the last acquisition, disbursed late Jan/early Feb 2026.
demand_pricing: IPM growth has moved to double digits in the last two quarters (earlier 7-9%), driven mainly by volume; management could not isolate a specific cause.
Management said it cannot forecast future IPM growth and built its organic forecast on a lower industry growth assumption.
Growth above market is attributed to wallet share gains from better fill rates, product availability, range and more principal collaborations.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 FY26 through preponed government/diagnostic PPP billing, which made the sequential inorganic contribution look lower.
Management said MedTech has limited distributor competition and offers more scope for demand-generation contracts with higher gross margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for the next 3-5 years without acquisitions, and what ROCE is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and sees ROCE of 25-30% possible at the end of that period.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the minority interest exist and when will the call options on it be exercised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said call options were agreed at deal signing at a valuation multiple matching the original acquisition, with exercise windows of 2-5 years; the minority is reinvested rather than paid out. Not all options fall due this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the sequential inorganic revenue contribution decline from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Q1 government project revenue was billed early in Q4 FY26 because of budget timing, so Q1 had a high base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 one-off items recurring in other opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only part of the INR11.5 crore one-offs sat in other expenses; run-rate other expenses of about INR55 crore are expected to be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 5% EBITDA margin be a floor for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 5% for the full year but said it targets quarter-on-quarter improvement and may revise guidance after H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did minority interest fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minority share depends on subsidiary profit; Q4 had a revenue preponement at one subsidiary that boosted its profit share (INR17 crore in Q4 vs INR14 crore in Q1).

risks_watch: Growth in IPM has been unusually strong for two quarters and management cannot explain the cause, so sustainability is uncertain.
Non-controlling interest is about 27% of PBT and call-option buyouts (2-5 year horizon) will need funding, possibly from parent or subsidiary cash.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 through government billing timing, so quarterly comparisons may be distorted.
Quarterly OCF is not disclosed; balance-sheet items (gross debt, net debt, OCF) will be given only at half-year and full-year, in September and March.
Interest cost is expected to stay at the Q1 run-rate after the INR200 crore debt drawdown.
Further exits of low-margin sub-distribution businesses could reduce reported growth again (about 2.5% impact in Q1).
544122|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top line and margins, and clear on the strategy to consolidate and grow organically. Management was evasive on IPM growth drivers, on the quantum of OCF and net debt, and on non-controlling interest funding.
key_quotes: We have started FY27 on a very strong footing. Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% year-on-year to INR1,940 crores.
We are pleased to have delivered our full year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance in the very first quarter of the year.
We always retain full operational and cash flow control over every one of these entities and minority share of profit is always reinvested in the business and not paid out.
When I say 50% of EBITDA getting converted to OCF, means EBITDA minus working capital changes, whatever is the remaining is supposed to be 50% of EBITDA.

We should not be looking at OCF on a quarter-to-quarter basis. We should be looking at an annual basis because -- and that's how I have given the guidance that on an annual basis, we will convert 50% of our EBITDA to OCF.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: New product launch

544122|2026-09.headline: Entero Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32.9% to INR2,087 crore; management says FY27 will beat its 23% growth guidance without quantifying it.
544122|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 32.9% YoY to INR2,087 crore in Q2 FY27, with organic growth of 18.2% and inorganic contribution of 14.7% from calendarised prior-year acquisitions. Gross margin rose 126 bps to 11.5% and EBITDA margin rose 135 bps to 5.3%, with EBITDA up 78% YoY. PAT was INR61 crore (up 66%), but operating cash flow was negative INR46.5 crore in H1 because a Maharashtra government payment of about INR55 crore slipped, lifting NWC days to 64. Management said H1 was ahead of internal plans and reiterated a 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion target, while flagging a one-off INR11.87 crore receivable write-off at a subsidiary.

segments.name: Pharmaceutical distribution
segments.commentary: Core business; organic growth driven by customer base expansion, wallet share gains and new product categories. Management says the company is gaining share ahead of industry growth. Exited certain low-margin accounts, which helped margins.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Management says MedTech is at 15%+ of total revenue. Analyst math implies about INR600 crore in H1, which management confirmed. Margin not disclosed; management says margin depends on value-add rather than product type.

segments.name: Government business
segments.commentary: About 2-3% of total revenue (management cited 3%). Long-standing supplier to government agencies and PSUs. Receivables from Maharashtra government contracts were delayed in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance (previously stated): consolidated revenue growth of about 23% excluding new acquisitions, EBITDA margin of 5%, and EBITDA-to-OCF conversion of 50%.
Management says it is 'very comfortable' to beat the revenue and margin guidance but did not give a revised number.
Calendarisation benefit from acquisitions will taper in Q3 and more so in Q4 unless new acquisitions close.
Interest cost of about INR20 crore per quarter should fall once debt repayments on last year's acquisition debt start in Q3.
Management is sticking with the 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion for FY27 and says FY28 guidance will come with Q4 results.
MedTech revenue will exceed INR1,000 crore in FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: No capex plans were discussed on the call.

Acquisitions: no acquisitions closed in H1 FY27. Management is evaluating several opportunities, including large deals in pharma and MedTech, with a minimum size of about INR100 crore and a preference for product-category expansion.
Net debt to EBITDA is capped at 2x by board mandate; surplus cash goes to acquisitions first, with debt repayment as the fallback.
H1 acquisition consideration paid was INR166 crore, all deferred consideration from earlier deals (March balance INR309 crore). Management did not give the remaining balance or its timing.
Call option exists on minority interest; NCI was about 25% of profit before minority interest in Q2 (INR15 crore). No number given for future buyout.
demand_pricing: Scale: over 92,200 retail customers and 2,900+ hospital customers in H1, about 500 districts across 20+ states and UTs, 90,400+ SKUs from 3,200+ manufacturers.
Management says it is gaining share and that the Indian healthcare products market is fragmented and growing at a double-digit pace.

Trade margin cap / NPPA action: 137 molecules notified; these account for about 2% of Entero's portfolio. Management says distributor margin percentages have not changed historically and that any MRP cut mainly hits hospitals and manufacturers.
Industry (IPM) growth reached about 15% in Q2 against a historical 7-10% range, mostly volume-led; management said it does not know the root cause.
A one-off INR11.87 crore receivable default at a subsidiary (pharmacy customer) was fully provided in Other Expenses; post-dated cheques and security are held and legal recovery is being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company upgrading the 23% revenue growth guidance given H1 growth above 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is in a very comfortable position to do better than guidance on growth and margin but gave no new numerical guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the proposed hospital MRP or trade margin caps hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no material impact is expected because distributors did not earn the gap; the 11.5% gross margin is all-inclusive, and the molecules notified so far are about 2% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Was the INR12 crore provision a margin drag, and what was the write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the margin would have been higher without it. It was a customer default at a subsidiary, the full INR11.87 crore is in Other Expenses, and part was already in the opening provision.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt repayment or minority buyouts reduce the minority share over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers. Operating cash flow will go to acquisitions, minority buyout or organic growth, depending on opportunities; debt is repaid only if no high-ROCE use is found.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 OCF conversion of 50% of EBITDA hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the 50% target for FY27 and said nothing much has changed since the guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach 20% in FY28 without acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will give FY28 numbers at Q4 results. It said organic growth is also a priority and that many organic opportunities are being worked on.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow: H1 OCF was negative INR46.5 crore; the Maharashtra receivable (about INR55 crore) was due in November, and NWC days must come down from 64.
Pricing regulation: NPPA trade margin caps on more molecules or hospital MRP changes could affect top-line prices even if margin percentage holds.
Receivable quality: INR11.87 crore subsidiary default, with recovery uncertain.
Acquisition timing: calendarisation benefit fades in Q3-Q4, so organic growth must carry the rate unless deals close; management said it hopes large deals will close this year.
Leverage and minority interest: board cap of 2x net debt to EBITDA; NCI absorbs about 25% of profit before minority interest.
544122|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on H1 growth, margins and the guidance beat, but deliberately vague on specific numbers for FY28, minority buyouts, acquisition size and the subsidiary write-off. Cash-flow timing was framed as a one-off.
key_quotes: What I said in my note, that we are in a very, very comfortable position to better than the guidance that we have provided.
So, any margin, any MRP reduction is not likely to have any impact on our overall margin structure.
Had this money been received on the due date, our H1 operating cash flow would have been positive.
The board, internally, we have this mandate that we will not exceed 2x net debt to EBITDA ratio.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose 135 bps to 5.3% and management says FY27 margin will beat the 5% guide, though calendarisation tailwind fades from Q3 and the INR11.87 crore write-off was a drag.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Organic growth of 18.2% (20% like-for-like) and management says it is gaining share in a fragmented market growing at double digits, though calendarisation benefit tapers from Q3.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 35% against FY27 guidance of about 23%, and management says it is 'very comfortable' beating both revenue and margin guidance, though no new number was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the beat and held the 50% OCF conversion target, but H1 OCF was negative INR46.5 crore and NWC days are 64, so cash-flow risk remains.

rows.label: Maharashtra government receivable (~INR55 crore) collection
rows.why: The payment was due in November and is needed to bring OCF back on track and cut NWC days from 64, though it slipped once already.

rows.label: Acquisitions closing (pharma / MedTech, min ~INR100 crore)
rows.why: No deals closed in H1 and several are under evaluation, with management hoping large deals close this year; calendarisation benefit fades in Q3-Q4 without them.

rows.label: NPPA trade margin caps on 137 molecules
rows.why: The notified molecules are about 2% of portfolio, so direct impact is small, but more molecules or hospital MRP cuts could hit top-line prices.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 growth, margin and beating FY27 guidance, and on the 50% OCF target, but vague on FY28 numbers, minority buyout, acquisition size and the write-off; analysts pushed on upgrade quantification and cash conversion.

544124|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% and EBITDA 26% YoY; management targets new products (poles, towers, guardrails) at 25-30% of revenue this year.
544124|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 16% YoY and EBITDA up 26%, with H2 revenue up 18% and EBITDA up 21%. The call centred on diversification: the Jharsuguda (Odisha) unit now produces highway guardrails, octagon and high-mast poles, and transmission line towers, with about 2,300-2,400 tons of tower orders on the books. Management said new products carry higher margins than pipe, but EBITDA margin remains around 4% today. Capex is limited to about Rs 10 crore in FY27, with no new debt planned, and CRISIL upgraded the rating from BBB to BBB+.

segments.name: Pipe (black and galvanized, water line)
segments.commentary: About 85% of revenue and the largest volume product; management ranks it lowest on margin per ton. Pipe installed capacity exceeds utilisation, with a 10-15% per year utilisation increase targeted; Jharsuguda pipe expected to reach about 60% in 1.5-2 years.

segments.name: Highway guardrail / crash barrier
segments.commentary: About 12% of revenue; Hyderabad order book about twice production capacity, and a second galvanizing line is being added there. Current crash barrier orders about 2,000 tons (about 1,000 each in Hyderabad and Jharsuguda).

segments.name: Transmission line towers
segments.commentary: Early-stage; about 2,300-2,400 tons of orders mainly from Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, with a target of 1,000 tons per month. Management says capacity and orders are roughly equal today; the orders are expected to clear in about two months.

segments.name: Octagon and high-mast poles / monopole
segments.commentary: Pole capacity about 150 tons, with machines arriving in about 10 days to lift it to 300 tons and a target of 500 tons per month this year. Order book about 300 tons, with orders being held for about 45 days; monopole certification expected by Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: New products (poles, towers, guardrails) targeted at 25-30% of revenue this year, versus 15% today.
Management said EBITDA margin should rise by at least 1% above the current 4%, and called its figures conservative; steel price swings and new-product pricing are the key variables.
Revenue target of around Rs 1,300-1,400 crore, with management calling this subjective; an analyst's FY28 Rs 1,700 crore reference was not confirmed.
Pole target of 500 tons per month; tower target of 1,000 tons per month; EBITDA margin on new products estimated at about 7-8%, not yet verified.
No new debt planned for FY27-28; capex about Rs 10 crore in FY27, to be spent only when demand is confirmed.
Jharsuguda galvanizing tank to be added in about 1-1.5 months; Hyderabad galvanizing expansion also underway.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 3,77,000 MT per annum: Maharashtra (Bombay) about 1,25,000 tons at 74% utilisation; Hyderabad about 96,000 tons at 67%; Jharsuguda is the growth site.
Galvanizing lines in Maharashtra and Hyderabad are described as running at about 100% of installed galvanizing capacity.
Jharsuguda: second galvanizing tank being installed in about 1-1.5 months (machines arrived, civil work ongoing); Hyderabad adding another galvanizing line for crash barriers.
Pole capacity to go from 150 to 300 tons with machines arriving in about 10 days, targeting 500 tons per month this year; monopole certification pending with CPRI.
FY27 capex about Rs 10 crore, to be spent only once demand is confirmed (for example, poles going from 500 to 800-1,000 tons).
demand_pricing: Pipe price: about Rs 52,000 per ton last year (black), now about Rs 65,000 per ton; management said steel prices could rise further if geopolitical tensions persist.
Order book: about 5,000 tons of pipe across all three units (about 2,000 Maharashtra, 1,800 Hyderabad), expected to be delivered within about 4 days.
Jindal Steel offtake agreement runs April 2023 to March 2029 with a minimum offtake of 1 lakh metric tons; the company produces ERW pipe for Jindal.

Middle East conflict raised transportation and furnace oil costs (galvanizing uses furnace oil); exports to Europe disrupted, with a shift to Australia shipped from Bombay. Management says costs are being passed through to customers so far.
Management says India demand is growing about 9% a year in utilisation, and the company has PWD registrations in Chhattisgarh and UP for poles and towers.
Management said that the new products are order-based, so they are less exposed to steel-price inventory swings than pipe.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected at the Rs 1,700 crore revenue level by FY28, given 4% today?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new products (monopole, octagon/high-mast poles, towers, guardrails) carry higher margins than pipe, so margin should exceed 4% by at least 1%; tower orders are at about Rs 10,000 per ton margin versus Rs 3,000-4,000 per ton on galvanized pipe.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA per ton on galvanized pipe (about Rs 3,000) well below some peers (Rs 6,000-7,000)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its figures are conservative and that the company makes water-line pipe, while peers make higher-margin API pipe and export, which Vibhor is not targeting.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and EBITDA contribution from new products in FY26, and what margin can they reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined an exact FY26 figure, saying the products are new; it targets 25-30% of revenue from new products and estimates new-product EBITDA margin at about 7-8%, not yet verified.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any impact from the Middle East war?
qa_highlights.answer: Transport costs and furnace oil prices have risen and are being passed on to customers; export to Europe is disrupted and redirected to Australia, but domestic demand is said to be healthy.

qa_highlights.question: What are the current order book and delivery timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipe about 5,000 tons (delivered within about 4 days); crash barriers about 2,000 tons (about one month); towers about 2,400 tons (about two months, given audit and inspection); poles about 300 tons (about 45 days).

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-off or inventory gain in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said inventory gains are a regular process since finished product prices are reset monthly, so there is no major exceptional item; management said steel price spikes around the US-Iran conflict may reflect in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for FY27, and what is the debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 10 crore of capex in FY27, to be deployed only when demand is confirmed, and no new debt, as existing financing is already in place.

risks_watch: Margin uplift from new products depends on pricing for a new entrant; management said current prices are not a premium, and the 7-8% margin estimate is unverified.
Steel price volatility; inventory gains on pipe could reverse, and management flagged the Middle East conflict as a driver.
Pipe utilisation is well below installed capacity (Jharsuguda target 60% in 1.5-2 years), and pipe remains about 85% of revenue.
Monopole certification from CPRI is pending, with expected clearance by Q2 FY27; several department permissions are still pending.
Export disruption to Europe, plus higher freight and furnace oil costs from the Middle East conflict.
Concentration: Jindal offtake agreement (minimum 1 lakh MT per year) and tower orders tied to a few state electricity customers.

Management was vague or deferred on hard numbers (FY26 new-product revenue, peak revenue at current capacity, product-wise margins), and attributed margin and revenue uncertainty to steel price volatility.
key_quotes: So, our target is to give this ratio, which is 85 right now for pipe, 80 to 85, we will bring it down to 75.
We are not increasing any debt at the moment.
We will do additional of around about Rs. 10 crore, FY27.
So, the agreement has been quite similar since 2003 to now, which is that we produce all our pipe for and we sell it to Jindal's.

544124|2026-06.headline: Vibhor Steel guides ~20% Q1 revenue growth, driven by Jharsuguda; Q1 pipe dispatch only 1,500 t against 1,800 t pipe order book.
544124|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 20% YoY, with growth coming almost entirely from the Jharsuguda (Odisha) plant, while Mumbai and Hyderabad were broadly flat versus last year. Order books for pipe, crash barrier, transmission line towers (TLT) and poles were described as well above normal, but the second galvanizing tank at Jharsuguda (expected around 1 September) is the binding constraint. Management said new-product contribution would start in Q2 and smooth out in Q3 and Q4. Figures on EBITDA, PAT and margins were not quantified in the call; the company also said it is planning a North India plant via a newly incorporated subsidiary, starting with crash barrier.

segments.name: Pipe (ERW black/galvanized)
segments.commentary: 83% of revenue. Jharsuguda pipe order book 1,800 t vs ~1,500 t dispatched in Q1; Mumbai order book 6,500 t (1,000 t on hold, ~5,000 t sold); Hyderabad pipe/galv orders ~2,000 t vs 1,000-1,200 t historical average.

segments.name: Crash barrier / highway guardrail
segments.commentary: 12% of revenue. Jharsuguda order book ~600 t and Hyderabad ~850-1,000 t; Jharsuguda crash barrier line is at maximum installed capacity, with another crash barrier line being installed.

segments.name: Transmission line towers (TLT)
segments.commentary: Order book ~2,000 t (MP ~1,500 t, Chhattisgarh 200-250 t, Maharashtra 50-60 t, plus Sikkim, Chennai). Installed capacity ~600-700 t/month; dispatch of 300-400 t expected in the current month. Power Grid approval (~2 months) pending.

segments.name: Poles (octagonal, high-mast)
segments.commentary: Order book ~250 t, equal to ~75-80% of pole installed capacity of 300 t/month. Last 3 months' max sales 80 t; targets 100 t this month, 200 t next month, 300 t by October.

segments.name: Other / RSJ pole / Monopole
segments.commentary: RSJ pole first order ~500 t, processed as job work with ~Rs 1 crore revenue; Monopole certification pending, expected Q3. Monopole has highest margin per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation at the Sundargarh plant, its total capacity and the timeline to full utilisation?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to grow revenue from east and north India?

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split by product?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipe 83%, crash barrier 12%, other products 5%. Management expects the percentage split to stay broadly similar while volumes of other products grow.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from Jindal Steel, and what is the reduction target?
qa_highlights.answer: Jindal accounts for ~80-82% of revenue. Management targets ~70% over time but gave no timeline, and said organic pipe growth would not be curbed. Pipe production has risen from ~1,500 t per month last year to ~3,000 t per month now.

qa_highlights.question: Which products earn the highest margins, and what is the crash barrier margin?

Some TLT and pole orders reportedly gave ~10% margin, overall margin ~2%, and crash barrier ~3%. Management said competition in TLT and poles should stay limited for 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 revenue outlook?

qa_highlights.question: How will the company win customers for the two other new Tritium products in the US and Europe?

qa_highlights.question: Does Exicom have OEM tie-ups for supplying chargers with vehicles?

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS offering and its scaling path over 3-5 years?

544133|2026-06.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.

Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR20.9 crore (8.8% margin), helped by operating leverage and richer mix. Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated EBITDA swung from breakeven in Q4 FY26 to a INR22 crore loss in Q1; what drove the sequential drop and when does breakeven return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q4 seasonality in Indian business and Tritium's low-cost acquired inventory eroding, lowering Tritium margins. It still expects Tritium EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 and consolidated breakeven within the next two quarters, without specifying Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: When will Tritium's doubled order intake convert to revenue, and is the 3x growth and Q4 FY27 breakeven target still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the USD20 million backlog as of 1 July plus new bookings and large strategic wins (double-digit million dollars, executing from calendar 2027 Q1) give confidence in 3x revenue growth and Q4 FY27 EBITDA breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: What is Hyderabad plant utilisation and where will it reach in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad was built for about 2x AC charger capacity and roughly 4,000 DC chargers. Utilisation is about 65% on DC chargers, close to 100% on AC chargers, 90-100% on DC power system lines, and close to 100% on PCBA and battery lines. AC charger monthly run rate is expected to rise about 50% over the next three months, and another AC line has been ordered.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV revenue mix and growth outlook, and why is the AC capacity figure inconsistent with the annual report (42,000 to 222,000 units)?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of revenue, with mix expected to stay similar or rise slightly. Management said the 222,000 figure is right and that 48,000 was single-shift, with the doubling based on double-shift operation; it will revert with an exact answer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone depreciation rise, and what is the Tritium capitalisation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone depreciation rose about 67% YoY to INR10.3 crore, with management attributing an increase of INR10-12 crore to the new plant. Tritium's higher depreciation reflects capitalised R&D and acquisition-related servicing costs, which management expects to be amortised over 5-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can EV charger market share and unit volumes be estimated from EV registrations, and why was standalone EV growth only 15% when AC demand is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a very high share of wallbox chargers but not portable chargers, and volume depends on whether OEMs bundle wallboxes. Its DRHP cited 60% wallbox share, and it estimates current wallbox share at north of 50%. The 15% standalone EV growth reflects Q4 DC charger pull-forward; AC may have grown about 30% and DC about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US Tritium factory capacity and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the US factory can service about USD100 million a year, about 2.5x the current ~USD10 million quarterly revenue, and it is running at about one-quarter of that today due to the ongoing turnaround.

544133|2026-09.headline: Exicom Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 21.3% YoY to ₹277 cr and consolidated EBITDA turned positive at ₹1.8 cr, while Tritium is being divested.
544133|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue reached ₹277 cr (up 21.3% YoY, 17% QoQ), with the EV charging segment crossing ₹100 cr for the first time at ₹206 cr (up 58.7% YoY). Standalone EBITDA rose to ₹25.6 cr at a 9.2% margin, and consolidated EBITDA swung to +₹1.8 cr from a ₹32.7 cr loss a year earlier. Consolidated PAT loss narrowed to ₹57.8 cr, held back by depreciation on the Hyderabad plant and Tritium amortisation. The board approved divesting 100% of Tritium, with a non-binding term sheet at an indicative enterprise value of $85 mn, targeted for December 2026 but possibly slipping.

qa_highlights.question: Why divest Tritium when it is approaching EBITDA break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the need for working capital and engineering investment to enter data-centre power infrastructure, plus higher capital needs for home-market and export growth. It called the decision difficult and said it was the best use of capital.

qa_highlights.question: Is the power-module manufacturing agreement exclusive, and what is its term and volume commitment?

544134|2026-03.headline: Platinum Industries Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 132 crore, EBITDA up 95% to INR 15.3 crore; FY27 guidance above 40% revenue growth.
544134|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 132 crore (+37% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 15.3 crore (+95%, margin 11.6%, +350 bps) and PAT of INR 14.8 crore (+164%). Full-year consolidated revenue was INR 450 crore (+15%), but EBITDA (INR 59.8 crore, +4.2%) and PAT (INR 51.2 crore, +3.7%) grew far slower. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth above 40% and a 35% CAGR over FY26-29, with the Egypt plant slated for Q3 FY27 and oleo chemicals sales starting April 2026. Raw-material inflation from the March geopolitical events created a temporary margin pressure that management expects to pass through over time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 margins were about the same as Q3; the dip came from March raw-material price rises. Margins are expected to hold if raw materials stabilise, with a time lag in passing costs on.

qa_highlights.answer: Sales started April 2026; FY27 target INR 55-60 crore, reaching run-rate by Q2; own plant to follow in about 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs jump and what senior hiring occurred?
qa_highlights.answer: Employees rose from about 120 in FY25 to about 150 now and about 170 in April 2026, plus senior hires to stabilise management; employee cost to sales up about 1 percentage point, expected to normalise once the new plant runs optimally.

544134|2026-06.headline: Platinum Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR 108.9 crore (from INR 115.4 crore) and PAT to INR 11.13 crore as Palghar ramp-up weighed.
544134|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue declined about 5.6% YoY to INR 108.9 crore while EBITDA fell to INR 13.44 crore at a 12.34% margin, versus INR 15.16 crore at 13.14% a year earlier. Standalone revenue grew about 7.3% YoY to INR 110.4 crore, but standalone EBITDA margin was 11.64%. The expanded Palghar facility only became fully operational on 21 May 2026, so the quarter carried ramp-up costs and lower lead-free PVC offtake. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% and kept Egypt commercial production targeted before 31 December 2026.
